26cec91dd0585550: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 8,690 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) candidates nationwide have benefited from the 2026 Tamil Language Excellence Empowerment Programme, involving an allocation of RM901,680.

The Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), under the Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma), said the programme was implemented in collaboration with the Education Ministry (MOE) to improve academic performance and Tamil language proficiency.

The initiative was part of the government's efforts to support students from the Indian community through focused academic preparation, while boosting their motivation, self-confidence and examination readiness, it said in a statement today.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said 7,897 SPM candidates and 793 STPM candidates who sat for the Tamil Language paper nationwide had benefited from the programme.

"We want to ensure every student has the opportunity to achieve excellence, regardless of their background. Through Mitra, we are not merely providing educational assistance, but implementing academic interventions that can directly impact student achievement.
"Tamil language is not merely a subject to be mastered for examinations, but a treasure trove of language, culture and identity that must be preserved by future generations," he said.
Ramanan earlier officiated the programme at the Omnia Auditorium, Menara BAC, Petaling Jaya, which was attended by nearly 300 SPM candidates and 50 educators from Selangor.

Mitra said it would continue to expand educational initiatives under Kalvi Madani, including through strategic collaborations with MOE, state education departments and relevant institutions, to extend access to targeted academic development programmes for more students from the Indian community.

0d009396bbd31890: AI datacenters are a rats nest of fiber optic cables stitching together thousands of AI accelerators, NICs, switches, and everything else required to train and run the latest and greatest modes. Cisco hopes to untangle this mess with a new pluggable optic developed in collaboration with Nvidia that will pack between four and eight times the bandwidth of existing pluggables into a single port. Announced at the Open Compute Project (OCP) global summit this week, the ultra-dense small form factor pluggable (USFP) promises to pack up to 32, 400 Gbps lanes into a pluggable roughly the size of existing OSFP modules. Each of these pluggables would boast 12.8 Tbps of Ethernet bandwidth, as much as a high-end enterprise switch just a few years ago. To put that in perspective, the most sophisticated pluggable optics today cap out at around 1.6 Tbps using eight 200 Gbps links. Such a pluggable has the potential to significantly simplify cabling across AI datacenters where it isn't uncommon for each GPU to be paired with an 800 Gbps and soon 1.6 Tbps NIC. A single USFP pluggable could consolidate eight GPUs worth of cabling into a single fiber optic bundle. Meanwhile, on the switch side, a future 204.8 Tbps switch would only require 16 USFP ports to support 128 1.6 Tbps endpoints. Cramming all that connectivity into a single pluggable won't be easy. Today a high-end pluggable optic might pull on the order of 20 watts. Cisco's USFP spec calls for up to 100 watts per pluggable. There are also design constraints that have to be taken into consideration. Four times as many links per pluggable means 4x as many electrical contacts that have to be perfectly seated. Because of this Cisco says USFP modules will employ a two phase insertion mechanism in which the pluggable is first inserted into the cage and then a second mechanism is actuated to make the electrical connection. Speaking of reliability, USFP would have a bigger blast radius than conventional pluggables. A single bad laser or digital signal processor (DSP) has the potential to take out far more than a single GPU, but entire systems. While that might sound bad, it's nothing compared to co-packed or near-package optics where one failure could drop an entire rack's worth of accelerators from the network. Nvidia's participation in the development of the USFP standard is notable as the Ethernet networking titan has largely moved away from pluggables in its most recent set of switches. Many of its Spectrum-X and Quantum-X switches now use co-packaged optics and for good reason. Cutting out the pluggables on the switch side nets a roughly 30 percent power savings. But while Nvidia's latest switches may use CPO, its NICs still rely on pluggables in part because it offers integrators greater flexibility. Not everyone is building 100,000-plus GPU clusters for training. For racks utilizing a top of rack switch, lower power direct attach copper cabling can be used without much issue. Given Nvidia's investments in CPO we can only speculate on its interests in USFP, but it likely comes down to densification. The AI infrastructure giant is rapidly moving toward 600 kW racks packing 144 GPUs on board. First teased in early 2025, Nvidia's Vera Rubin Ultra platform promised 115.2 TB/s scale out bandwidth per rack or about 3.2-6.4 Tbps of bandwidth per GPU package depending on whether they're counting bidirectional bandwidth or not. It just so happens that Cisco's initial USFP spec calls for 16, 400 Gbps links per pluggable, or about 6.4 Tbps of bandwidth. While Cisco and Nvidia may be leading the charge on the development of an ultra dense optical pluggable, like most things Ethernet, USFP will be an open standard anyone can use in their designs. Microsoft taps Cisco for multi-datacenter AI Alongside Cisco's latest tie up with Nvidia, Switchzilla also revealed that Microsoft is now using its Silicon One P200 routing chips to distribute workloads across multiple datacenters. Nvidia and others have taken to calling this kind of multi-site computing: scale across networking. We discussed Cisco's datacenter-scale routing platform at length late last year, but the silicon competes directly with products like Nvidia's Spectrum-XGS and Broadcom's Jericho 4-based offerings. Cisco touts the P200 as the first 51.2 Tbps systems "deployed in a production environment by leading hyperscalers." With enough qualifiers you can be the first at anything. As we reported at the time, Microsoft was among the first major hyperscalers to embrace scale-across networking as a means of overcoming local power constraints with its Fairwater clusters in Wisconsin and Georgia. And it seems we finally know the hardware good old Redmond is using to stitch them together. Cisco gives SONiC some love Speaking of hyperscalers, one thing you probably won't find in a hyperscale network is Cisco's Nexus network operating system (NOS). Hyperscalers like Microsoft typically employ vendor agnostic NOS platforms to avoid vendor lock-in and make managing networks across multiple Ethernet vendors cheaper and easier. Originally developed by Microsoft and later open sourced, SONiC is among the most popular and widely deployed of the hyperscale NOSes. SONiC support, we should note is nothing new for Cisco which contrary to popular belief is more than willing to sell you any one piece of its networking stack, assuming you've got a big enough purse — the hyperscalers certainly do. As such Cisco is one of the biggest contributors to the SONiC project. Instead of forcing customers to use its software stack, Cisco's approach to SONiC and the hyperscale is to extend the NOSes capabilities to better take advantage of ASIC's unique capabilities and allow for integration with its services. At OCP this week, Cisco announced support for its Live Protect platform in SONiC to make it easier for customers to keep up with security patches in the wild. This capacity is expected to roll out next year. ®

67c337361c252a45: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia should negotiate with Disney Cruise Line to make Langkawi or Penang a departure and arrival hub for its Disney Adventure cruise ship, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Yeo Bee Yin (PH-Puchong) said Malaysia should aim to become more than just a port of call by allowing international tourists to begin or end their cruises at either destination.
"I don't think we should be content with merely being a port of call.

"I propose that the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry begin strategic negotiations with Disney Cruise Line to explore the possibility of making Langkawi or Penang an official embarkation and disembarkation port," she said when debating the 2027 Budget.
Yeo said the arrangement could encourage tourists to spend several days in Malaysia before or after their cruise, benefiting the local tourism industry.
"Imagine the economic spillover. Tourists who begin or end their cruises in Langkawi could spend several days there before or after their voyage," she said.
She said Disney Adventure, which operates out of Singapore, was scheduled to make its first stop in Langkawi during a four-night cruise departing Singapore on Dec 31.
Yeo estimated that the ship, which can accommodate between 6,000 and 6,700 passengers, could make 25 to 30 visits a year, potentially bringing 150,000 to 200,000 passenger movements to Langkawi.
She said spending of between RM250 and RM400 per passenger could generate an estimated RM35 million to RM80 million in direct annual spending on the island, benefiting local businesses.
"However, the main question is whether these tourists will come ashore and spend money, or simply remain on board," she said.

Yeo said lengthy immigration queues and severe traffic congestion could discourage cruise passengers from disembarking, adding that immigration authorities had a crucial role in ensuring smooth arrivals.
She also called for upgrades to international airports to accommodate growing tourist demand and urged the ministry to pursue the proposed arrangement with Disney Cruise Line.

a810beec56da4fb4: KUALA LUMPUR: United Malacca Bhd has announced that its executive director Datuk Seri Tee Lip Sin has passed away at the age of 55.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the plantation company said Tee began his career as an executive at Prosper Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd in 1995 before rising to become an executive director.
He was the group managing director of Prosper Group and a director of Prosper Capital Holdings, a substantial shareholder of United Malacca.

Tee also served as a director of Australia-listed PRL Global Ltd, Phosphate Resources (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, Phosphate Resources (Singapore) Pte Ltd and several private companies involved in plantation and milling businesses.
He held a Master of Business Administration from the University of Sunderland and a degree in Business Administration from the University of Wales.
Tee held 1.98 million United Malacca shares directly and 179,700 shares indirectly, through his spouse and children.
His death came two days after United Malacca announced a mandatory general offer (MGO) at RM6.10 a share by Prosper Trading Sdn Bhd, Tee Kim Tee and Tee Cheng Hua.
The offer followed Prosper Trading's acquisition of a 13.44 per cent stake in United Malacca from Great Eastern Life Assurance (Malaysia) Bhd for RM171.93 million.
United Malacca shares were halted an hour after the announcement before closing unchanged at RM6.04, valuing the company at RM1.27 billion.

c148546747af667f: ATHENS: Greece's conservative government on Wednesday sought to distance itself from the shock ouster of US ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle, with a senior official insisting relations with Washington are unaffected.
"These are issues that concern the US and do not affect Greek-American relations," deputy prime minister Costis Hatzidakis told state TV ERT.
"This is not the first time that there are no ambassadors, in Greece or other countries in Europe, representing the US or other states for some months," he said.

US president Donald Trump forced Guilfoyle out of the administration on Tuesday, amid allegations she sought money from one of his supporters and accepted lavish hospitality from wealthy Greek businessmen.
The move came days after a visit to Athens by state secretary Marco Rubio.

Guilfoyle, 57, a former Fox News host and ex-fiancee of Trump's eldest son, had faced mounting scrutiny following a series of reports by The Wall Street Journal about her financial dealings and relationships with wealthy businessmen.
The Journal reported that she asked Eric Deters, an influential Trump supporter, to pay off US$100,000 in personal credit card debt shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing in July 2025.

The Journal also reported that Guilfoyle boasted of luxury trips and hotel stays funded by wealthy Greek businessmen, citing hundreds of messages, emails and other records, including recorded conversations.
In Athens, there was particular outrage after a Journal report last month alleged Guilfoyle stated that the US could organise "political change" in Europe.
“We can do that to any country we want. We can do that here," she allegedly said at a March dinner attended by Greek and American officials.
The Greek government said it had "never" been threatened or pressured, and the foreign ministry said it was "unnecessary" to summon Guilfoyle on the issue.

The main opposition party's foreign affairs spokesman, Dimitris Mantzos in a statement, said the reports "essentially confirm a model of transactional diplomacy, far removed from the principled foreign policy that our country ought to be implementing".

"Do the government and the prime minister intend to take any initiative or make any representation to the US, or will they be content to watch the country being offered as a 'theatre' for economic and business battles of (private) interests?" Mantzos said.
The US embassy's deputy chief of mission Josh Huck, a career diplomat, is expected to take charge in the interim, Greek reports said Wednesday.
In a statement on X, Guilfoyle rejected the allegations against her and defended her record as ambassador, highlighting efforts to boost US energy exports and strengthen security ties with Greece.

8fd56e1d3bede61a: ISTANBUL: IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva on Wednesday urged governments to urgently strengthen public finances, warning that the global economy's resilience to repeated shocks is reaching its limits, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

Speaking at a press briefing during the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Georgieva said energy and fiscal buffers were being depleted, while persistent inflation and rising interest rates were adding to debt-servicing pressures.
Global growth is projected at about 3.1 per cent in 2026, unchanged from April's forecast but below last year's 3.4 per cent, she said.
The outlook reflects opposing forces, with the war in West Asia disrupting energy supplies while demand linked to artificial intelligence supports economic activity.
Economies integrated into AI supply chains, including Thailand, Malaysia, South Korea and Singapore, were generally performing better, along with energy exporters unaffected by wars.
Low-income countries and fragile states, particularly energy importers excluded from the technology boom, faced the greatest pressures.
Georgieva said government bond yields in advanced economies had risen to multidecade highs, reflecting inflation, investment demand, expectations of stronger AI-driven growth and fiscal weaknesses.
Higher benchmark yields were increasing borrowing costs for emerging markets even where their risk premiums remained stable, she said, warning that elevated financing costs were likely to persist.
Debt-servicing costs in low-income countries had increased from 6 per cent of government revenues a decade ago to 14 per cent, she added.

Georgieva urged governments to raise revenues, rationalise spending and improve public financial management. Assistance to offset rising food and energy costs should be temporary and targeted at vulnerable people while preserving price signals.
Central banks should remain focused on price stability, with the strongest case for tightening in economies where inflation exceeds targets and activity remains robust.
On global imbalances, she called on China to boost domestic consumption, the US to increase savings and reduce deficits, and Europe to strengthen investment.
US economic growth alone would not deliver the required fiscal adjustment quickly enough, making additional measures necessary, she said.
Georgieva also warned that disappointing near-term AI returns could trigger a disorderly market correction, while AI-enabled cyberattacks posed risks to financial stability.

a012801be71e97e9: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia masih tidak mempunyai strategi jelas memanfaatkan kecerdasan buatan (AI) bagi mentransformasikan ekonominya serta menambah baik penyampaian perkhidmatan kerajaan, kata bekas ketua penerangan Umno, Shahril Hamdan.

Shahril berkata, peruntukan Belanjawan 2027 bagi penggunaan AI kurang memperincikan bagaimana pembiayaan itu akan diterjemahkan kepada hasil yang bermakna kepada perniagaan dan ekonomi secara menyeluruh.

Beliau berkata, bajet itu merangkumi 100,000 langganan AI percuma untuk golongan belia pada tahun hadapan serta RM30 juta di bawah dana pemerkasaan AI diuruskan Perbadanan Ekonomi Digital Malaysia (MDEC) bagi membantu 4,000 perusahaan mikro, kecil dan sederhana (PMKS) mengguna pakai AI.

Namun, Shahril mempersoalkan sama ada pembiayaan tersbeut mampu membawa perubahan signifikan, sambil menekankan peruntukan RM30 juta itu jika dibahagikan hanya bersamaan sekitar RM7,500 bagi setiap syarikat.

"Dan saya pun tak tahu apa sebenarnya pengkhususan perincian RM7,500 lebih ini yang akan dibelanjakan oleh MDEC," katanya dalam audio siar Keluar Sekejap bersama bekas ketua Pemuda Umno, Khairy Jamaluddin.

Shahril turut menyuarakan kebimbangan inisiatif AI itu akan mengikut jejak langkah geran terdahulu yang bertujuan membantu perniagaan mendigitalkan operasi mereka, di mana impak pembiayaan berkenaan tidak dipaparkan dengan jelas.
"Kita ada 'headline figure', tapi kita tak tahu sebenarnya apa yang dibuat untuk bantu mengadaptasi AI," katanya.
Shahril membandingkan pendekatan Malaysia dengan ikhtiar Singapura dalam menarik syarikat serta bakat di barisan hadapan perubahan teknologi untuk beroperasi di sana.
Beliau memetik Anthropic, OpenAI, dan ElevenLabs sebagai contoh syarikat AI yang telah bertapak di Singapura.

"Saya rasa di Pulau Pinang dengan Kulim (Kedah) kita buat 'packaging' dan 'testing' ke atas cip. Tetapi, tidak menjana satu tenaga yang boleh membawa kepada segala macam bentuk pembinaan atas aplikasi dan juga atas kecerdasan yang kita 'host' di sini."
Bagaimanapun, Shahril berkata aktiviti tersebut masih belum menghasilkan momentum sama untuk membangunkan aplikasi dan keupayaan AI di peringkat tempatan.
"(Keupayaan AI) memerlukan satu syarikat...satu kerajaan, satu kementerian yang benar-benar memahami apa yang dia nak daripada AI untuk Malaysia," katanya.
Shahril berkata, Singapura mempunyai jawapan yang jelas mengenai apa yang mahu dicapainya dalam sektor AI, namun beliau mempersoalkan sama ada pemimpin Malaysia mempunyai kejelasan serupa.
"Saya tak pasti Malaysia, kalau kita tanya mana-mana menteri pun, PMX pun, dia tahu apa yang dia nak daripada AI Malaysia. Saya tidak fikir begitu," katanya.
Katanya, Malaysia sebahagian besarnya mendapat manfaat daripada kesan limpahan, termasuk pelaburan dalam industri berkaitan semikonduktor, pasaran modal, dan pelaburan langsung asing.
Tetapi, beliau berkata kerajaan masih belum menzahirkan strategi jelas menggunakan AI untuk mentransformasikan ekonomi dan menambah baik penyampaian perkhidmatan awam.
"Tetapi, bagaimana ia nak merevolusikan ekonomi kita dan penyampaian kerajaan kita, tak nampak strategi itu. Dan belanjawan ini tak membantu ke arah perkara itu."

df6e6c9b223d4cbc: PONTIANAK, Oct 14 — Every few years, residents of Indonesia’s West Kalimantan province contend with devastating wildfires that emit a noxious haze causing illnesses, shuttering schools and stifling economic activity.
Now, they’ve had enough.

Lawyers have filed a class action case claiming “negligence, omission and failure” on the part of the government that has resulted in “a massive public health crisis” in the province on Borneo island.
Their target: President Prabowo Subianto and 26 officials from the national, provincial and local government, as well as police and emergency services.

“We’re not asking for anything excessive. We’re only demanding our basic rights as citizens: clean air and a healthy environment,” Sisilius Rami told AFP at his home in the haze-blanketed city of Pontianak.
“We... want to breathe fresh air, see clear skies and enjoy the sun,” said the 29-year-old, one of four plaintiffs in the case.
Sisilius said the haze affects every aspect of daily life, disrupting schooling and outdoor activities including some farming. Anyone venturing outside must wear a mask or risk inhaling toxins.

“Children have the right to an education. The community has the right to live healthily. The government should be present to guarantee those rights, not leave people to face the consequences on their own,” he said.
The other plaintiffs are NGOs representing youth, environmental and Indigenous causes in a province with nearly six million inhabitants.
They “are all residents of the province of West Kalimantan affected by the 2026 haze disaster, whose number is so large it would not be practical to file claims individually”, the filing said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A motorist drives past a wildfire in the Bukit Batu area of Palangkaraya, Central Kalimantan province on October 13, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Limited means’
For weeks, communities in West Kalimantan have been fighting fires that have razed vast expanses of land and befouled the air as far away as Malaysia and Singapore.
The government has deployed firefighters assisted by volunteers across affected areas, and used cloud-seeding and water-bombing, with limited success.
For the AMAN Indigenous people’s NGO, also a plaintiff, too much of the burden has fallen on individuals armed with little more than garden hoses and surgical masks.
“If the government had truly been serious about extinguishing the fires, there would be no haze anymore,” said AMAN representative Tono, who like many Indonesians has only one name.
The government should have drilled borewells, distributed sufficient firefighting equipment and deployed more water-bombing planes to communities, Tono said.
“The government has far more adequate resources and facilities than the community. Yet on the ground, it is the community that is fighting with limited means.”
The group’s lawyer, Glorio Sanen, said the Indonesian state did not prepare adequately despite having had months of warning of a particularly intense dry season due to the El Nino weather phenomenon.
“Who has the authority to lead and coordinate across ministries and levels of government? The president. That is why we have named the president as a party to the case,” he said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
This aerial picture shows smoke shrouding the Equator Monument and the city of Pontianak in West Kalimantan on September 17, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Environmental criminals’
The plaintiffs want the government to declare a national emergency to release resources for fire containment and recovery.
They are also suing for free health services for people laid low by acute respiratory infections, and compensation for the families of those who died from it.
“We don’t want communities to continue to be victims year after year, while the same problems recur without fundamental improvements,” the lawyer said.
“This lawsuit is our way of asking the state to fulfil its obligations.”
The plaintiffs also want a thorough investigation into the causes, and point the finger at large corporations burning land to cultivate timber, rice and palm oil, or for mining.
“This haze disaster has caused extraordinarily heavy losses. In education, in health, in the economy. As a consequence of this disaster, we must uncover who bears responsibility,” Glorio said.
“We must not allow environmental criminals, arsonists who burn forest and land areas, to remain at large and unpunished while the number of victims keeps growing and their suffering worsens.”
The government told AFP it “respects” the legal action, and that “many of the concerns raised by residents are already being addressed through ongoing efforts”.

These include “ground and aerial firefighting, healthcare services for affected communities, and investigations into 95 corporations” whose activities may have contributed to the fires, the Government Communications Agency told AFP.
It highlighted a standing prohibition on land-clearing by burning, and said the government shared the plaintiffs’ goal of “clean air and an end to recurring forest and land fires”.
Sisilius is not convinced, pointing to previous major fires.
“This has already happened in 2015, it happened again in 2019, and it has happened again in 2026, in a very severe way,” he said.
“We hope the state truly shows up.”
The next court hearing is scheduled for October 21. — AFP
800f0803baed49cc: WASHINGTON, Oct 14 — Pope Leo XIV had a cancerous tumour surgically removed from his right lung yesterday in a 90-minute operation described as “successful” by the Vatican.
Here are what several medical experts told AFP about the surgery and diagnosis.
What is pulmonary adenocarcinoma?
Pulmonary adenocarcinoma, the type of tumour removed from the Pope, generally comes from “a primary cancer,” said Dr. Juanita Mora, a medical spokesperson for the American Lung Association.
She told AFP that “is a good thing” because it means the tumour is from lung cancer instead of generating from the spread of another cancer.

There are two main types of lung cancer: “small cell” cancers, which spread aggressively and make up about 10 to 15 per cent of diagnoses, and “non-small cell” cancers, which make up the vast majority.

“Adenocarcinoma is the most common kind of what’s called non-small cell lung cancer,” David Spigel, a medical oncologist specialising in lung cancer research at Nashville’s Sarah Cannon Research Institute, told AFP.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Candles, flowers and prayers are led at the statue of John Paul II outside Rome’s Gemelli University Hospital, where Pope Leo XIV has been admitted for an operation to remove a lump from his lung October 13, 2026. — AFP pic
Promising outlook

David Carbone, director of the Oncology Centre at Ohio State University, noted that while smoking is the most well-known risk factor for a lung cancer diagnosis, “most lung cancers that we diagnose today are in people who haven’t smoked, or (stopped) many years ago.”

Lung cancer is the top cause of cancer death worldwide, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO), but the prognosis can vary significantly depending on the type of lung cancer and how advanced it is when first detected.
“When we look at five-year survival rate from lung adenocarcinoma, and it’s nicely localised, the rate is approximately 63 to 67 per cent,” Mora said.
“But if we catch it early, it becomes 80 to 98 per cent, especially after surgical removal.”
In such a case, the patient “will achieve a cure and never have their life threatened by cancer,” Spigel added.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

A cardboard cutout of Pope Leo XIV is displayed inside the main church in Saٌa, in the Lambayeque region of northern Peru, on October 13, 2026. Pope Leo XIV had a cancerous tumour surgically removed from his right lung on October 13, in a 90-minute operation described as ‘successful’ by the Vatican. — AFP pic
A standard procedure
Pope Leo XIV announced the presence of the lung nodule on Sunday, saying it had been “detected at a very early stage” and was localised.
The Vatican said “the lower lobe of the right lung was removed” during Tuesday’s operation to remove the mass.
“He had part of his right lung taken out, which is the standard procedure,” Carbone told AFP.
“There’s a lot of reserve in the lung, and people can have an entire lung removed and live a normal life,” he added.
“I would expect that he’d be back to completely full level of activity very soon.”
What now?
The question now is whether Pope Leo XIV will need additional treatment such as chemotherapy or radiation.

According to the experts consulted by AFP, the answer will depend on several factors, such as the size of the cancerous mass removed, how aggressive it was, its genetic characteristics, and whether or not it has spread.
A Vatican source indicated that additional testing is underway.
For Carbone, the fact that the Pope has already undergone surgery is encouraging.
“Because if it had spread to, for example, the lymph nodes in the centre of the chest, he would have had some treatment before surgery, which he didn’t have,” he explained.
“They really do go straight to surgery only for the earliest stage tumours, which makes me think this was a very early stage tumour, and has a quite good prognosis.”
He stressed that treatment for lung cancer has improved considerably over the past few decades, “and the prognosis is better than ever. So I would be hopeful for a full recovery.” — AFP
5b9ab8f235add309: NEW DELHI, Oct 14 — For more than three decades, a stretch of road in central New Delhi was where Indians came to be heard, staging rallies to press their demands and hold those in power accountable.

Trade unions, retired soldiers, anti-corruption campaigners, women’s rights groups and student activists all protested beside the capital’s iconic 18th-century Jantar Mantar observatory, drawn by its location near the city’s commercial heart and the seat of political power.
But this week, the country’s most recognisable stage for public dissent officially lost its status as an authorised protest venue, prompting concerns among activists over shrinking democratic space.
“Jantar Mantar as a protest venue has been de-notified,” Delhi Police said in an order issued Monday, without providing a reason.
The move comes days after a confrontation between authorities and anti-government protesters led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) online movement.

The youth-led group has mobilised thousands to take to the streets over a revision to electoral rolls that critics say could disenfranchise eligible voters, months after separate protests over exam irregularities forced the education minister to resign.

While authorities have designated three alternative demonstration venues in Delhi, campaigners say visibility and proximity to lawmakers are central to the right to protest in the world’s largest democracy.
“Jantar Mantar is in the centre of the town, it is connected, it is next to parliament... it was a very important space for all protests,” human rights activist Shabnam Hashmi told AFP.
“This is nothing but a move to curb dissent.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Security personnel detain a demonstrator during a protest demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities linked to the ‘special intensive revision’ (SIR), near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi October 11, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Spirit of resistance’
Jantar Mantar, meaning an instrument to calculate in Sanskrit, is designed for the observation of astronomical positions with the naked eye.
The roughly 1.6-kilometre (one-mile) street next to Jantar Mantar became synonymous with protest after being designated a demonstration site in 1993.
In July, thousands of students led by the “cockroach” movement gathered there before attempting to march towards parliament over irregularities in competitive examinations.
For nearly a month, Jantar Mantar transformed into a vibrant hub of Gen-Z dissent, its walls transformed into canvases for angry slogans, defiant messages and graffiti challenging the government.
Tensions resurfaced this month when police denied permission for a CJP protest at the site demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner over the contentious voter roll revision.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Delhi Police personnel stand guard ahead of a protest by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner over alleged ‘special intensive revision’ (SIR) voter-roll irregularities, near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi October 10, 2026. — AFP pic
Yesterday, a day after authorities formally de-notified the site, police detained CJP leaders who clambered over the barricades to “reclaim Jantar Mantar”.
“Jantar Mantar is not just a location but a spirit of resistance that nobody can ever take away,” the group’s founder, Abhijeet Dipke, said.
The developments have reignited debate over where citizens can now take their grievances.
Activist Hashmi said protests at Jantar Mantar had already become increasingly restricted in recent years through limits on space and timings.
But its location, she said, made it uniquely effective because demonstrators could easily reach parliament, government ministries and media houses.
“In a democracy, you require spaces where you can protest,” she said.
“This is absolutely unacceptable.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Delhi Police personnel barricade a street ahead of a protest by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner over alleged ‘special intensive revision’ (SIR) voter-roll irregularities, near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi October 10, 2026. — AFP pic
Neighbours complain
Authorities have said demonstrations can be held at two venues on the capital’s outskirts, while a third site closer to the centre, Ramlila Maidan, remains available for larger gatherings.
But activists argue that moving protests away from the city centre risks reducing turnout and visibility, particularly for campaigners travelling from distant states.
Greater transport costs, longer journeys and reduced media attention could all diminish the impact of demonstrations, they say.
Some of those living in the Jantar Mantar neighbourhood, however, welcomed the police order.
“Roads leading to our homes are barricaded, there is noise and garbage, and our daily lives are disrupted,” Varun Seth, a resident, told the Hindustan Times newspaper.
Former Delhi Police commissioner Kiran Bedi also defended the move, saying Jantar Mantar’s “sensitive” location made it poorly suited to hosting protests.
“Every city does require an open space for democratic expression... but forgets to provide for (it),” she said on social media.
A protester told AFP yesterday that demonstrators would continue to gather at Jantar Mantar despite the police order.
“With great resolve, we will carry out civil disobedience,” she said.
“We will sit here and protest,” she added, before being whisked away by police as she attempted to march towards the site. — AFP
09670f68a29eae2f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Early detection and immediate medical intervention remain paramount in managing Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA), an autoimmune condition that can affect children as young as eight months old, a medical expert said.

However, low public awareness of the condition often results in delayed diagnosis, potentially leading to irreversible joint damage in affected children, according to Sunway Medical Centre, Sunway City’s (SMC) paediatric rheumatologist Dr Cham Weng Tarng.

“JIA is an autoimmune condition that affects children below the age of 16. The youngest patient we have seen was in late infancy, and the disease can affect any joint in the body,” he told Bernama in an interview at SMC.
Dr Cham said a diagnosis of JIA requires persistent joint inflammation for at least six weeks, after other possible causes, such as localised infections and malignancies, have been ruled out.

He said JIA is classified into seven subtypes - systemic arthritis, oligoarthritis, rheumatoid factor-negative polyarthritis, rheumatoid factor-positive polyarthritis, psoriatic arthritis, enthesitis-related arthritis and undifferentiated arthritis - which can affect one or more than four joints.
Dr Cham said detecting JIA in infants and toddlers posed a particular challenge as young children were often unable to articulate their physical discomfort.
“Younger children are sometimes unable to express that they are in pain, so parents usually notice it from the way their child moves, like walking with a limp or refusing to walk,” he said.
He said symptoms could be subtle, recounting a case in which an infant’s hip arthritis was detected after the child repeatedly cried in distress whenever the nappy was changed.
For older, active children who frequently fall or sustain sports-related injuries, Dr Cham advised parents to seek medical evaluation if joint pain or swelling persisted for more than a week.
He said parents should not dismiss such symptoms as ordinary childhood injuries, as persistent pain or swelling could indicate an underlying condition requiring medical attention.

Dr Cham said a major challenge in managing JIA was the misconception among some parents that their children were exaggerating their symptoms or being difficult, which could delay diagnosis and critical treatment.
He highlighted the case of a patient who became wheelchair-bound at the age of 11 after discontinuing medical treatment for five years, allowing the condition to deteriorate severely.
Once the joints are damaged by arthritis, we cannot reverse it. So, what we try to do is maintain function and mobility,” he said.
Dr Cham said the delayed intervention had led to severe joint deterioration and left the child’s bones extremely fragile, increasing the risk of fractures even from falls.

Beyond joint destruction, Dr Cham warned that children with JIA were also at risk of developing uveitis, an inflammatory eye condition that requires regular monitoring and management by an ophthalmologist.

Despite the debilitating risks of late-stage JIA, Dr Cham emphasised that the medical landscape for the disease has undergone a massive technological revolution offering a highly optimistic outlook for all diagnosed patients.

“Previously, in the 1950s, the only medications we could give children were painkillers and steroids. But now, there are many more latest medications such as, disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs,” he said.
These include conventional anti-rheumatic medications alongside biological therapies that utilise advanced antibodies to ‘switch off’ internal inflammation without relying solely on steroids.
With controlled and early treatment, Dr Cham assured that children with JIA can achieve sustained improvements, allowing them to lead unrestricted lives.

Dr Cham advised parents of children with newly diagnosed JIA to place their trust in modern medical science, maintain strict adherence to prescribed medication regimes and foster open communication with their treating physicians.

He added that medical facilities with dedicated children emergency department may also be able to provide point-of-care investigations together with on-site dispensing pharmacy to support coordinated paediatric care including for JIA cases.

“Treatment of JIA now is more advanced and there are opportunities for recovery. There is a light at the end of the tunnel. So, there is hope. The most important thing is to seek for treatment as soon as they noticed the early signs,” he said. — Bernama

5ecd2f74ed4316b2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Chinese fashion label Cabbeen returned to the Shishi coast in Fujian province for the third year running last month, staging an open-air seaside runway that featured a musical contribution from Malaysian composer Mac Chew.

55d53c4726624bb1: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Gautham Vasudev Menon took about 4,000 fans on a nostalgic journey through his 25 years in cinema on Saturday night, in a first-of-its-kind, café-style concert built around storytelling and the enduring songs from his films.

Rather than simply handing the stage to his singers, the filmmaker stayed at the centre of it for almost the entire three-hour show at The Arch Galeries, narrating the stories behind the music as it was performed.

He set the tone from the start, opening with a line from Robert Frost’s poem The Road Not Taken. It was a fitting choice for a director who has spent his career carving out a storytelling style that is distinctly his own.

The evening’s title, Ondra Renda — 25 Years of GVM, comes from a song in his 2003 film Kaakha Kaakha. That film featured prominently alongside Minnale, Vettaiyaadu Vilaiyaadu, Vaaranam Aayiram, Vinnaithaandi Varuvaayaa and Neethaane En Ponvasantham, as Karthik, Saindhavi, Blaaze, Krish, Haripriya, Sathya Prakash and Adithya RK took turns at the microphone.
Behind them, scenes from each film played on the screens, so that every song arrived with the characters and moments fans had come to remember.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Radaan Mediaworks chairperson and managing director Radikaa Sarathkumar and actor R. Sarathkumar enjoying the performances. — Picture courtesy of My Events International
Star turns and personal tributes

Shruti Haasan’s appearance was brief, but she electrified the hall with “Adiyae Kolluthey”. Paal Dabba then shifted the energy entirely with “His Name Is John”, from Gautham’s still-unreleased Dhruva Natchathiram.

Gautham, popularly known as GVM, was not content to only narrate. He sang a number of songs from his own films and paid tribute to the figures who shaped him, among them composer Ilaiyaraaja and filmmaker Mani Ratnam.
Between performances, he gave the audience a rare look at how he works, recalling his collaborations with Ilaiyaraaja, Harris Jayaraj and AR Rahman.

There was a local touch too. Gautham referenced Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s rendition of “Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat” at the BRICS summit in India last month, before turning to a Hindi song that ranks among his own favourites.
He brought the night to a close with a reflection on the place art holds in people’s lives.
“Medicine, engineering, all that is important for the human race. But poetry, art, music – this is what we live for. And I truly believe that music and lyrics can change the world,” he said.

Shruti Haasan performs ‘Adiyae Kolluthey’ during the live show. — Picture courtesy of My Events International
Beyond the stage

The celebrations did not stay on stage. A video from the concert has since gone viral on social media, showing director Lingusamy dancing energetically to “Ava Enna Enna Thedi Vantha Anjala” from Vaaranam Aayiram. J
Joining him were Radikaa Sarathkumar, chairperson and managing director of Radaan Mediaworks, and her husband, actor R. Sarathkumar.
The concert was organised by My Events International Sdn Bhd in collaboration with Chennai-based Radaan Mediaworks India Limited, with the concept created by Oru Oorile Oru Film House.

The two companies have formed a strategic collaboration aimed at bringing more Indian cinema and entertainment projects to Malaysia, including live events, celebrity appearances and film-related programmes.
Under the arrangement, My Events International will provide local market knowledge and event execution, while Radaan contributes its experience in Indian television, cinema and media production.

01d02e5412a03a49: KUALA LUMPUR: Infomina Bhd's net profit rose 30.6 per cent to RM10.55 million in the first quarter ended Aug 31, 2026 (Q1 FY27), from RM8.08 million a year ago.
The increase was mainly due to higher profit contribution from the technology infrastructure operations, maintenance and support services segment, the group said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
Quarterly revenue rose 39.5 per cent to RM76.19 million from RM54.63 million previously, driven by higher revenue contribution from the same segment.
Earnings per share increased to 1.76 sen from 1.34 sen previously.

Infomina's outstanding order book stood at RM614.2 million following contracts secured in Malaysia from the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and a local financial institution, as well as a contract from Panasonic Digital Co Ltd in Japan.

The group also completed the acquisition of a 51 per cent stake in Blue Fortress Sdn Bhd, which is expected to strengthen its cybersecurity, digital transformation and managed technology services businesses.

Separately, Broadcom appointed Infomina to distribute and support its mainframe software portfolio in 12 Asia Pacific markets, including four new markets: Australia, New Zealand, South Korea and India.
The group already operates in Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Hong Kong, China and Japan.
Overall, the board remains optimistic about the group's outlook despite ongoing global economic uncertainties, barring unforeseen circumstances.
It said the recent developments, together with disciplined execution, were expected to support the group's growth.
842dc2881d1089db: Some of America's biggest tech companies have a warning for Europe: curb your reliance on US cloud providers, and it could cost you €115 billion. That's the finding of a new study commissioned by CCIA Europe, a lobbying group whose members include Amazon, Google, and Meta, companies that have plenty of reasons to want European governments to keep buying American cloud services. The research, conducted by the European Centre for International Political Economy (ECIPE), claims the European Commission's proposed Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) could saddle Europe with €115 billion in costs over the next decade, more than six times the Commission's upper estimate of €18 billion. The report argues that restrictions favoring European cloud providers would leave governments and businesses facing hefty bills to migrate workloads and rewrite software. It puts direct public-sector costs at €33.3 billion, with a further €80 billion potentially falling on private companies in sectors including banking, healthcare, energy, and transport. However, a rather large asterisk is attached to that €80 billion figure. It assumes the Commission extends sovereignty requirements beyond public procurement to cover 25 percent of cloud workloads in essential private-sector industries. In other words, it's a modeled scenario, not a bill Brussels has already handed European businesses. The study also comes with some baggage of its own. CCIA represents several US technology giants that dominate the European cloud market, including Amazon and Google. Both have spent years selling European customers cloud services while more recently developing sovereign cloud offerings designed to address concerns about foreign ownership, data access, and regulatory control. Amazon, for example, has been developing its AWS European Sovereign Cloud, while Google markets a range of sovereign cloud solutions. Apparently, sovereignty is an attractive proposition when it comes with a hyperscaler logo attached. Meta, another CCIA member, has its own interests in European AI infrastructure, although it is not a commercial cloud provider on the scale of AWS or Google Cloud. The report specifically targets Article 31 of the proposed legislation, which it says could allow the Commission to extend sovereignty requirements into essential private-sector services. CCIA argues that forcing businesses to move away from existing cloud infrastructure could trigger expensive software redevelopment projects, with code rewriting and re-architecting accounting for 69 percent of its estimated costs. Luxembourg would apparently take the biggest hit, with the study putting the cost at €1,711 per worker over ten years. Denmark (€905), Austria (€900), and Finland (€864) also face hefty bills, as does Ireland (€856), which hosts the European headquarters of several US tech giants. CCIA is urging EU governments to overhaul the proposed legislation, limit sovereignty restrictions to sensitive workloads, and abandon requirements based on corporate origin or personnel nationality in favor of what it calls risk-based technical safeguards. "Member States cannot rely on the Commission's incomplete estimates when deciding CADA's strict sovereignty requirements for cloud and AI providers," said Mitchell Rutledge, CCIA Europe's policy manager. "Taxpayers and businesses will foot the bill, yet the official assessment missed 70 percent of CADA's true impact." For AWS and Google, offering European customers greater control over their data also helps retain business that might otherwise migrate to European competitors. It's a rather convenient arrangement: sell customers sovereignty on one hand, while an industry association representing your interests warns governments against imposing too much of it on the other. Neither company responded to The Register's questions. Whether Europe's sovereignty ambitions will prove as expensive as CCIA predicts is unclear. What's easier to establish is that the companies warning Brussels about the cost of reducing its dependence on US technology have plenty to gain if Europe decides to keep buying American. ®
e4d19c30fd53cd7f: LONDON: Global stocks rose on Wednesday, helped by a steadying in AI-related shares and government bonds, as investors kept volatility to a minimum ahead of US inflation data later in the day.

Tech shares in Europe were among the top performers of the day, taking their lead from a recovery overnight in Asia, where Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix both closed up, and from an upbeat outlook from Dutch chip equipment maker ASML, whose shares rose 1.4%.
Europe's STOXX 600 was up 0.5%, while the MSCI All-World index edged up 0.1%.

Sentiment remained cautious, however, as oil prices rose following attacks on two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and after Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying new tactics to target ships, raising the risk of fresh disruption to energy supplies.
Brent crude futures, which are around their highest in nearly two weeks, were last up over 0.5% on the day at US$106.4 a barrel.
"Geopolitics and AI remain the main drivers of the market. There seems to be little progress on the geopolitical front, with a deal looking less likely before the midterms.
"We have been in the optimistic camp, but have to admit that chances of even a fudge look low," Jefferies strategist Mohit Kumar said.
Government bonds also witnessed some respite after a few weeks of almost non-stop selloffs, in the face of high energy prices and rising expectations for global interest rates to keep edging up.
The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes dipped 1 basis point to 5.21%, nearing its lowest in two weeks, while 30-year yields were steady at 5.56%, following three days of declines.
Another round of earnings is due from the big banks, starting with Bank of America on Wednesday, which saw profits fall in the third quarter.
US bank stocks lost ground on Tuesday after mixed quarterly earnings results from Citigroup and several competitors, which weighed on the broader market.
S&P 500 futures were up 0.1%, while those for the Nasdaq were down 0.2%.
CPI test awaited
Investors were awaiting the release on Wednesday of the US consumer price index for September, which is expected to have picked up, given the strength of energy and other commodity costs last month.
Economists estimated headline inflation accelerated to an annual 3.6% in September due to rebounding energy prices, with the core CPI rising 0.2% on a monthly basis.

Right now, money markets show traders are attaching a roughly 20% chance of a hike from the Federal Reserve (Fed) late this month and a near-100% chance of a rise in December. Wednesday's inflation data could help refine those odds.
New York Federal Reserve president John Williams said the Fed may need to raise its policy rate once more this year to slow inflation, but that he saw no need for hikes in 2027.

"With several FOMC members indicating that a pause is likely this month amidst a moderation in job creation, we doubt that inflation numbers would be sufficiently hot to change the odds of hiking materially," Eugene Leow, senior rates strategist at DBS, said in a note.
The US dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six others, was up 0.1% at 102.26, close to its highest since April 2025.
The euro was down modestly at US$1.118, while the pound was steady at US$1.326.

Meanwhile, in China, data on Wednesday showed producer prices rose at their fastest pace in more than four years, while consumer inflation edged up last month, although weak domestic demand kept the increase in broader price pressures contained.
30e4ff45b8cbb59d: KUALA LUMPUR: The expansion of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) from 30 to 50 constituents is expected to provide a more accurate representation of Malaysia's domestic economy.
The impact on the weightings of existing constituents is expected to be manageable, according to AHAM Asset Management Bhd (AHAM Capital).

Its deputy head of equity (Malaysia), David Loh, said the expansion would provide broader coverage of the domestic market, which has long been represented by a relatively small number of companies, while allowing the performance of more sectors, particularly technology, to be reflected in the benchmark index.

"For the longest time, the biggest comment about the Malaysian index is that it is very much in the old economy sector. A lot of technology stocks have done well in the past, but their performance was not captured in the FBM KLCI because they were not in there.

"With these technology stocks coming in, that will help the new index going forward," he told Bernama on the sidelines of a media engagement and networking session with AHAM Capital fund managers here today.
The implementation will take place from Dec 21, 2026, with Phase 1 seeing 20 new constituents added to the FBM KLCI at 50 per cent of their final index weight.
In Phase 2, the 20 new constituents will reach 100 per cent of their final index weight, completing the transition to the enhanced FBM KLCI effective June 21, 2027.
Loh said the phased implementation was intended to minimise market disruption as the inclusion of 20 new constituents would dilute the weightings of the existing 30 constituents.
"Based on the early calculation by the index strategist, the impact on their weightings should not be more than a high single digit," he said.
He added that the transition was designed to minimise disruption and that the overall impact was expected to be manageable.
Following the expansion of the FBM KLCI, the FBM 70 will be reduced from 70 to 50 constituents and renamed the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Mid Cap Index.
The FTSE Bursa Malaysia Top 100 Index will remain unchanged at 100 constituents.
cbdf5ae2b3aeb026: PETALING JAYA: Sekolah-sekolah akan ditutup apabila bacaan Indeks Pencemaran Udara (IPU) mencecah 200, manakala semua aktiviti luar bilik darjah mesti dihentikan sekiranya bacaan melebihi 100 susulan ketetapan Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM) yang kembali mengguna pakai dasar jerebu sedia ada.

Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek berkata, pihaknya menyambut baik penegasan Agensi Pengurusan Bencana Negara (Nadma) bahawa sebarang langkah menangani jerebu perlu berpandukan Pelan Tindakan Jerebu Kebangsaan.
"Sehubungan itu, KPM telah memulakan penyelarasan tatacara pengoperasian sekolah berpandukan PTJK,” katanya menerusi hantaran di Facebook.

"Langkah ini bertujuan memastikan keputusan dibuat secara lebih tersusun berdasarkan penilaian keadaan semasa, termasuk bacaan IPU dan nasihat kesihatan daripada Kementerian Kesihatan Malaysia (KKM)."

Fadhlina mengakui bacaan IPU boleh berubah dalam tempoh singkat, dan tindakan menutup sekolah beberapa hari lebih awal tanpa mengambil kira faktor berkenaan boleh merugikan masa pembelajaran murid walaupun kualiti udara telah pulih.

Bagaimanapun, katanya, ibu bapa tetap dibenarkan tidak menghantar anak ke sekolah jika bimbang akan tahap kesihatan dan keselamatan mereka sepanjang musim jerebu, dengan syarat pihak sekolah dimaklumkan terlebih dahulu.
"Keselamatan dan kesihatan anak-anak tetap menjadi keutamaan kita. Namun, setiap hari persekolahan juga mempunyai nilai yang besar terhadap perkembangan dan pembelajaran mereka," katanya.
Beliau berharap penyelarasan itu dapat memberi kepastian lebih jelas kepada ibu bapa sekali gus meringankan kesulitan yang dihadapi mereka.
Menurut dasar kementerian pada 2019, sekolah perlu ditutup apabila bacaan IPU mencecah 200, tertakluk kepada pengesahan jawatankuasa pengurusan bencana daerah.
Bagaimanapun, sepanjang episod jerebu kali ini, KPM memperkenalkan ambang penutupan sementara berdasarkan bacaan IPU.
d1207a064413d0f9: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia lacks a clear strategy to harness artificial intelligence to transform its economy and improve government service delivery, former Umno information chief Shahril Hamdan said today.
Shahril said the 2027 budget allocation for AI adoption lacked sufficient details on how the funding would translate into meaningful outcomes for businesses and the wider economy.

He said, the budget included 100,000 free AI subscriptions for young people next year and RM30 million under an AI empowerment fund managed by the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) to help 4,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) adopt AI.
However, Shahril questioned whether the funding would bring about meaningful change, noting that the RM30 million allocation worked out to approximately RM7,500 per company.

“I do not know what the specific details are, or precisely how MDEC intends to spend that RM7,500 per company,” he said in the latest episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast with former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin.

Shahril said he was concerned that the AI initiative could follow the pattern of previous grants intended to help businesses digitise their operations, where the impact of the funding was not clearly demonstrated.
“We have the headline figure, but we do not know what is actually being done to help businesses adopt AI,” he said.
Shahril contrasted Malaysia’s approach with Singapore’s efforts to attract companies and talent at the forefront of technological change to establish their operations there.

He cited Anthropic, OpenAI and ElevenLabs as examples of AI companies that had established bases in Singapore, saying the country had positioned itself to attract businesses operating at the forefront of technological development.
“Malaysia, meanwhile, has a presence in the AI supply chain, particularly through data centres and semiconductor packaging and testing operations in Penang and Kulim.
However, Shahril said these activities had yet to generate the same momentum for developing AI applications and capabilities locally.
“What I am trying to say is that we need a real strategy. We need a company, a government or a ministry that genuinely understands what it wants to achieve with AI in Malaysia,” he said.
Shahril said Singapore had a clear answer to what it wanted to achieve in the AI sector, but questioned whether Malaysia’s leaders had the same clarity.
“I am not sure Malaysia does. If we asked any minister, even the prime minister, what Malaysia wants to achieve with AI, I do not think they would have a clear answer,” he said.
He added that Malaysia was benefitting largely from spillover effects, including investments in semiconductor-related industries, capital markets and foreign direct investment.
However, he said the government had yet to articulate a clear strategy for using AI to transform the economy and improve public service delivery.
“When it comes to how AI can revolutionise our economy and improve government service delivery, I do not see a clear strategy,” he said.
“And this budget does not help move us towards that goal.”
d205dfd9de7affa6: KUALA LUMPUR: LLØØPP, a brand-new audiovisual format created by Dutch-American artist and composer 0010x0010 (Ray Tijssen), has launched at REXPERIENCE (RXP.KL), the immersive digital art gallery inside REXKL.
Produced by SQNXR and presented alongside Jazzy Group, the showcase marks the format's very first residency.
Rather than running as a standard exhibition, LLØØPP gives a single room three distinct personalities throughout the day.
Its three programmes—MORNING, DUSK, and DANCE—each pair an original 10-minute musical score with generative visual art created from that exact music.
As the music plays, the visuals loop continuously around the room.

This creates a space that completely changes its mood without changing its physical structure: transforming from a place to breathe and stretch, to a place to eat and talk, and finally into a place to dance.
The official launch on Nov 7 will showcase all three experiences in a single day.
MORNING presents afternoon yoga and meditation, while DUSK features early-evening dining with a specially curated menu.
DANCE is a late-night electronic music session featuring a live performance by 0010x0010.
Because each programme runs on a continuous loop, visitors can enjoy a single cycle or stay through multiple loops during their booked session.
"A room can hold different energies without changing its architecture," said 0010x0010 in a statement yesterday.
"With LLØØPP I compose the music and the visual world together, so each programme changes how the space feels and how people use it. You can return to the same room and find a different experience."
Designed for long-term use in immersive venues, cultural hubs, and hospitality spaces, the format gives audiences a fresh reason to keep coming back.
"Kuala Lumpur audiences move between wellness, food and nightlife in a single evening, and REXKL is where those worlds already meet," said Jazzy Group CEO Joanne Goh.
"LLØØPP lets one room serve all three. It is the natural home for the format's first residency."
Tickets are now available on Cloudjoi for RM45 per entry at www.cloudjoi.com.
2d5d9216c417f720: GEORGE TOWN: Penang's RM114.8 million Sungai Pinang flood mitigation project is 50.86 per cent complete, with full completion scheduled for Sept 20, 2027.

State Infrastructure Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the project aimed to reduce flash flood risks across the 51sq km Sungai Pinang river basin, where rapid development had placed increasing pressure on existing drainage infrastructure.

"The project is expected to reduce the flood-affected area in parts of the Sungai Pinang basin by 10.15 per cent, while reducing damage to public infrastructure, residents' properties, housing and transport links," he said during a visit to Phase One of the Sungai Pinang river basin flood mitigation plan.
The project, which began on Sept 21, 2023, is designed to provide flood protection against events with a 100-year average recurrence interval.
Its scope includes deepening and widening a 1.4km stretch of Sungai Pinang, constructing 1.02km of parallel drains and upgrading drainage outfalls to improve stormwater flow towards the sea.
The works also include a piano weir and a pumping station equipped with four screw pumps, two on each riverbank, each with a capacity of 2.0 cubic metres per second.
An ancillary building is also being constructed.
The 3.2km Sungai Pinang serves as the main drainage channel for the river basin in Penang's northeast district, discharging water into the sea.

Rapid development in the surrounding catchment has altered land levels and surface water flows, while the existing drainage system has struggled to cope with higher water volumes, particularly during heavy rainfall, increasing the risk of flash floods.

Zairil said the state government remained committed to ensuring the project was implemented effectively and would continue to monitor its progress to ensure its flood-reduction objectives were achieved sustainably.
"The project is expected to help minimise flood-related losses and strengthen protection for communities and infrastructure in vulnerable parts of the basin," he added.
724837ab3f2eb1c9: LONDON: Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has been fined £25,000 (US$33,000) by England's governing Football Association (FA) after he claimed officials would "not let Manchester United lose".
Arbeloa made his remarks following Fulham's 1-1 draw with United in the Premier League at Craven Cottage in September.
Matheus Cunha equalised for visitors United in the 89th minute.

Arbeloa, who admitted the charge, has also received a warning for his comments, with the FA saying the Spaniard "acted in an improper manner by making comments in a post-match interview that imply bias and/or question the integrity of a match official".
London club Fulham are currently bottom of the Premier League with just two points from their opening six games.
712c1da95e490606: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has begun coordinating school operating procedures based on the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) to ensure that decisions on school closures are made in a more systematic manner, taking into account Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and health advice.

Its minister, Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, said that under the coordinated procedures, outdoor activities would be postponed when the API reading exceeds 100, while schools would be closed when the reading exceeds 200, in accordance with the PTJK.
“We need to understand that API readings can change within a short period.

“Closing schools several days in advance without taking these changes into account could result in children losing learning time even after air quality has returned to normal,” she said in a Facebook post today.
She said the ministry welcomed the National Disaster Management Agency’s (NADMA) emphasis that haze management must be guided by the PTJK, following discussions with relevant agencies.

At the same time, Fadhlina said she understood the concerns of parents who have to wait for daily decisions on school operations while the country faces haze, particularly those whose children have health problems or are more sensitive to air pollution.
As such, she said parents could keep their children at home if they were concerned about their health and safety during the haze, provided they notify the school authorities.
“The safety and health of our children remain our top priority. However, every school day also matters for their development and learning.

“I hope this coordination will provide greater certainty for parents, reduce the difficulties they face and ensure that every decision on school operations takes into account both the health of children and the continuity of their education in a balanced manner,” she added. — Bernama
ddc3c70065a3b3de: KUALA LUMPUR: Singer and sape player Alena Murang hopes traditional sape music will one day be recognised as a mainstream genre in its own right, rather than being confined largely to cultural and tourism events.

"I hope music made by sape could one day be taken as mainstream music all by itself," said Alena, 37, who is collaborating with the Malaysian Philharmonic Orchestra for an upcoming concert titled Concerto for Sape and Orchestra.
While the traditional Bornean string instrument has gained increasing attention, she noted that it still occupies a space between different musical genres and settings.
"It's usually played at a lot of government functions, such as cultural or tourism events, or where representation is needed," she said.

"While we're grateful for this opportunity, I personally hope that one day it can be acknowledged as music by itself, and that is why I'm thrilled for this collaboration with the MPO," she added at a press conference held here earlier today to announce the concert.
Scheduled for Oct 31 at Dewan Filharmonik Petronas, the evening will feature the world premiere of a specially commissioned 20-minute composition for sape and orchestra.
Sabah-born musician Vivian Chua composed the piece, with Alena performing the solo part alongside the MPO.
Alena admitted to feeling both excited and nervous about bringing the composition to life, particularly because its structure differs from the familiar verse-and-chorus format of popular music.
"I'm both nervous and excited to see how we can bring this piece together," she said, adding that memorising the lengthy work would present another challenge.
The collaboration marks another milestone in Alena's musical journey with the orchestra.

She previously performed with the MPO two years ago for its Sounds of Borneo concert, and hopes the upcoming performance will help introduce the sape to wider audiences while demonstrating its potential far beyond traditional cultural settings.
712abe6dbfeae186: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 (Bernama) — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended a donation to Makkal Osai senior editor Rajan Boopalan, who is undergoing treatment at Selayang Hospital after suffering a blood clot in his head.
Anwar said several officers from the Prime Minister’s Office had visited Rajan at the hospital on his behalf.

“Besides enquiring about his condition and conveying my regards, they also handed over a contribution on my behalf to ease the burden on him and his family during his treatment,” Anwar said in a Facebook post today.
He also prayed for Rajan’s speedy recovery and for his treatment to proceed smoothly.
Anwar expressed hope that Rajan would fully recover and that his family would be given the strength to get through this challenging period.
Rajan was previously reported to have been found unconscious at his home before further examinations confirmed that a blood vessel in his head had ruptured.
He subsequently underwent a surgical procedure to remove the blood clot, and his condition is now reported to be stable as he receives further treatment. — bernama
31789286c139bbef: KUALA PILAH: Disputes over royal succession in Negeri Sembilan must be resolved in accordance with adat or customary law and legal provisions, rather than personal interests.

Negri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir said the authority of the royal institution must be upheld through integrity, justice and responsibility, warning that actions contrary to established customs could undermine public confidence and threaten the state's stability.

He said said Adat Perpatih and the law formed the foundation of the position of the Ruler and succession to the throne in Negri Sembilan, while adat institutions, including the Undang Yang Empat, Lembaga, Ibu Soko, Buapak and Anak Buah, represented an important heritage passed down through generations to preserve traditions and maintain stability.

"Those who, over the past several months, have taken actions that sparked disputes over succession rules in the name of defending adat must understand that adat cannot be defended by violating its own rules.

"Such actions not only risk undermining the authority of customary institutions and the palace but could also destabilise the state and erode public trust," he said in his royal address at the installation ceremony of Datuk Azrin Khairi as the 17th Undang of Jelebu at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here.

The ceremony was also attended by Tunku Ampuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin.
State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and heads of state government departments were in attendance.
Tuanku Muhriz said the authority of the institution of the Ruler depends on respect for adat, the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.

"The high and noble position of the Ruler comes with a great trust and responsibility. The trust of the people, in turn, is an essential foundation for ensuring that this institution continues to be respected and preserved.

"As the Malay proverb says, Raja adil raja disembah, raja zalim raja disanggah (a just ruler is revered, a tyrannical ruler is opposed); justice and integrity must always be the foundation of leadership.
Tuanku Muhriz urged all parties to learn from history and not allow personal interests to override truth and justice at the expense of the state's security, well-being and longstanding heritage.
He said adat is not merely a heritage to take pride in, but a trust that must be preserved and defended with full responsibility.

"Indeed, the future and stability of Negeri Sembilan depend on the readiness of all of us to respect adat, to obey the law, and to place the interests of the state above personal interest, for the sake of generations to come," he said.

His Royal Highness concluded by expressing hope that Negeri Sembilan Darul Khusus continues to be at peace and prosperous, with its institution of monarchy, its adat heritage and the unity of its people always preserved. — BERNAMA
e06d042fc6839b68: LONDON, Oct 14 — Pierre Sage has admitted in an interview with AFP that the opportunity to manage in the Premier League was one he could simply not refuse as he prepares to return to his native France with Crystal Palace this week.
Palace are in Europa League action tomorrow at Lyon, a special fixture for Sage who got his coaching break there in late 2023 and enjoyed a whirlwind 14 months in charge.

Sage, 47, has now joined a small band of Frenchmen to have managed in the Premier League, following most notably in the footsteps of legendary former Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger and the late Gerard Houllier, who was in charge at Liverpool.
“I am the 10th French coach to have worked in the Premier League and the slightly crazy thing is that I am the first to have done so without having had 100 matches as a manager,” Sage said.
“Arsene Wenger and Gerard Houllier did incredible things here,” he added. “When the opportunity comes along you obviously say to yourself that it might not come up again.”
Sage had no top-level management experience when he was appointed Lyon coach in November 2023 by their American then-owner, John Textor — who also formerly held a significant stake in Palace.
The seven-time former French champions were bottom of Ligue 1 and heading for relegation.
Sage transformed their fortunes so remarkably that they ended up qualifying for Europe and reaching the French Cup final.

Yet he was sacked halfway through the following campaign. There were talks with English second-flight club Queens Park Rangers that came to nothing before he bounced back in spectacular fashion last season at Lens.
Under Sage, the side from far northern France won the French Cup for the first time in their history and came second in Ligue 1 behind all-conquering Paris Saint-Germain.
Unsurprisingly his achievements attracted interest, and a new chance arose to move to England as Palace sought a successor to Oliver Glasner.
‘Historic’ achievements
“It was a difficult decision because we had such an incredible year (at Lyon) — historic even — that I could sense what kind of impact it might have,” he told AFP.
“But at some point, you also have to think of yourself and that is what led me to my decision.”
Sage, who was a goalkeeper at amateur level, worked his way up the coaching ranks to become the head of Lyon’s youth academy before getting his big break.

He is learning all about the differences between French football and the Premier League, beyond the enormous financial gulf — Palace’s resources now far outstrip those of Lyon, who have fallen on harder times amid a wider economic crisis in Ligue 1.
Palace lost their first two matches under Sage, but their form has picked up since and they are fresh from beating Nottingham Forest 3-1 last weekend.
The Eagles, who won last season’s Conference League, started their Europa League bid with a 4-0 victory over Poland’s Lech Poznan.
“Compared to France, matches are always played at the same level of intensity by both teams,” Sage said of his early impressions of the English game.
“It is very rare that a team sits back, tries to shut down the spaces and lets you play.”

The very fact this fixture is being played is somewhat ironic — Palace won the Conference League last season having been barred by Uefa from competing in the Europa League due to Textor’s involvement with them and Lyon.
Lyon were allowed to play in the continent’s second-tier competition, and do so again this season after falling short in the Champions League preliminary rounds.
“The first thing I dreamed of when I left Lyon was that I hadn’t left at all,” Sage joked as he contemplated tomorrow’s game.
“Being sacked is part of the job. It was more leaving Lyon that was difficult for me.”
Now focused on his new life in south London, Sage is optimistic Palace can remain competitive domestically and also go far in Europe.
“With the quality we have, if we rotate the squad in the right way we can compete in both competitions,” he said. — AFP
1071fb5c1ab13829: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
The US military’s race to make fake blood

In February 2007, a US military helicopter carrying blood to a field hospital was shot down in Iraq, killing all seven crew members. The mission was a reminder of the risks of transporting blood, which has a limited shelf life and is often in short supply.

Now, a $73 million DARPA effort aims to create shelf-stable versions of plasma, platelets, and red blood cells. The idea is to develop dried blood products that can be stored for long periods and deployed quickly on the battlefield.

The project aims to have bags of dried blood products deployed in the field by 2029. But getting it all done will be tough, and researchers still have major questions about the safety and effectiveness of synthetic alternatives.
Discover how the military hopes to make blood last longer.
—Andrew Rosenblum

MIT Technology Review Narrated: Weight-loss drugs show signs of slowing biological aging, say drugmakers
Popular weight-loss drugs may do more than help people shed pounds. They might also slow the aging process.
Drugmakers Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk say patients taking their GLP-1 drugs age less quickly, according to molecular “aging clocks” that track changes in DNA or levels of key proteins.
