618120d1382c46f8: After a week’s delay, the new version of Python, v3.15, has been released. With it comes a proper profiler, an experimental just-in-time compiler, and a tightening of dictionary structures. It also offers a time-saving Lazy Import option for programs to not load modules until needed, the implementation of which ironically halted this release until a few last-minute regressions were sorted. But of all these new delicacies spread before the Pythonistas, the data wranglers of the bunch may most appreciate default UTF-8 support across all platforms. And when we say “all platforms,” we’re really just throwing shade at Windows (as usual). Python has defaulted to macOS and Linux Python environments for some time now. It’s a small but important update. About half of all Python developers use the language for processing and analyzing data, and about 58 percent of Python users build on Windows, according to various Python Software Foundation surveys. Party crashers Earlier versions of Python defaulted to the host system's locale encoding. This led to much consternation for Windows developers whose scripts opened UTF-8-encoded data sets, only to have non-ASCII characters corrupt or crash the program. Culprits could be as innocuous as a smart quote or a fancy apostrophe. Managed by The Unicode Consortium, with the help of the IETF and ISO, UTF-8 is an 8-bit binary encoding of the Unicode catalog of all the world’s written symbols. ASCII offered only 128 characters to cover the world’s knowledge, but UTF-8 provides over 1.1 million slots, which is plenty of room for smart quotes, emojis, musical and math notations, all the Chinese dialects, and even a few extinct languages (for research purposes). There’s also UTF-16 and UTF-32, but UTF-8’s combination of efficiency and inclusiveness made it the default for the Web and most modern operating systems. By the time Python Enhancement Proposal 681 was proposed in 2022 to make UTF-8 the preferred encoding, the language was already behind the times. That year, Java settled into UTF-8 with JDK 18, and Ruby 3.0 defaulted to the encoding scheme in 2020. Today all the cool languages and runtimes pledge allegiance to UTF-8, including Rust, Go, and Node.js (JavaScript itself prefers UTF-16 for internal encoding). Most code editors, from Visual Studio Code to Windows Notepad, prefer UTF-8. Data sharing and configuration formats such as JSON, TOML, and YAML all require 8-bit encodings. Python had long understood UTF-8, but programmers had to put a flag in their code alerting the language to use it – if they knew they had to do so at all. Many didn’t and were left scratching their heads over why their data processing scripts worked just fine on MacOS or Linux but then would flame out on Windows (or some other obscure system that defaulted to a C/POSIX locale). Programmers love puzzles To acquaint developers with the new aspects of the language, longtime Python programmer Barry Warsaw (AKA “Uncle Barry”) created a terminal-based adventure game called “whatsnewt” that offers 18 puzzles, each one built on a new feature found in Python 3.15, including a puzzle for UTF-8 support, “The Encoding Tower of Babel.” Once you've downloaded Python 3.15, do a “pip install whatsnewt” and then run the game on the Python command line. It even works on Windows, we hear. ®

Tuanku Muhriz said Adat Perpatih and the law formed the foundation of the position of the Ruler and succession to the throne in Negeri Sembilan, while adat institutions, including the Undang Yang Empat, Lembaga, Ibu Soko, Buapak and Anak Buah, represented an important heritage passed down through generations to preserve traditions and maintain stability.

“Those who, over the past several months, have taken actions that sparked disputes over succession rules in the name of defending adat must understand that adat cannot be defended by violating its own rules.

“Such actions not only risk undermining the authority of customary institutions and the palace but could also destabilise the state and erode public trust,” he said in his royal address at the installation ceremony of the 17th Undang of Jelebu at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here today.

The ceremony was also attended by Tunku Ampuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin.
State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and heads of state government departments were in attendance.
Tuanku Muhriz said the authority of the institution of the Ruler depends on respect for adat, the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.

“The high and noble position of the Ruler comes with a great trust and responsibility. The trust of the people, in turn, is an essential foundation for ensuring that this institution continues to be respected and preserved.

“As the Malay proverb says, Raja adil raja disembah, raja zalim raja disanggah (a just ruler is revered, a tyrannical ruler is opposed); justice and integrity must always be the foundation of leadership.
His Royal Highness urged all parties to learn from history and not allow personal interests to override truth and justice at the expense of the state’s security, well-being and longstanding heritage.
Tuanku Muhriz said adat is not merely a heritage to take pride in, but a trust that must be preserved and defended with full responsibility.

“Indeed, the future and stability of Negeri Sembilan depend on the readiness of all of us to respect adat, to obey the law, and to place the interests of the state above personal interest, for the sake of generations to come,” he said.

His Royal Highness concluded by expressing hope that Negeri Sembilan Darul Khusus continues to be at peace and prosperous, with its institution of monarchy, its adat heritage and the unity of its people always preserved. — Bernama
d5fbf92e9bd1cf2a: LONDON: Oil prices rose on Wednesday after an attack on the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, while Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying new tactics to target ships, seeking to keep oil prices high and influence US midterm elections.

Brent crude futures rose 91 cents, or 0.9 per cent, to US$106.60 a barrel at 1110 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude rose US$1.65, or 1.8 per cent, to US$95.79 a barrel, its highest in more than two weeks.

"Attacks on ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz and military strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis are supporting prices as market participants remain concerned about lower oil exports from the region," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, adding that exports had held up so far.
Iranian officials declined to provide details of the new strategy to target ships, but one said Iran had started using different offensive tactics about 10 days ago.

"That Iranian officials are openly admitting to undermining US efforts to keep oil prices under control speaks volumes about the real intentions behind the so-called 'peace talks'," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova.

The Iran-allied Houthis attacked an administrative building belonging to state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in the city of Dhahran, causing a limited fire, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on Wednesday.

The group has fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia over the past week in retaliation for the kingdom's support of Yemeni government forces. Riyadh's international airport has been hit four times, with a strike on Saturday killing 13 people.

Meanwhile, a container ship sank in waters south of the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine and catching fire, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said in a statement shared by state media on Wednesday. This came a day after the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a container ship and a tanker had been hit by unknown projectiles within the strait.

"The expectation that increased Russian diesel exports will ease market tightness is likely to limit sharp price movement in either direction," said Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment.

US President Donald Trump announced last Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war in Ukraine.

Russia's crude oil production increased by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million barrels per day but remained 870,000 barrels per day lower year-on-year, the International Energy Agency said on Wednesday.

The IEA also said that a lack of operational Russian refinery capacity meant the recently announced easing of Russian diesel export restrictions was unlikely to bring any material change to the global gasoil market balance.
Constrained diesel supplies could persist well into next year, the IEA also said.
d77edc20c0a7d645: PETALING JAYA: Schools will close when the air pollutant index (API) reaches 200, while outdoor activities must stop when readings exceed 100, as the education ministry returns to its long-standing haze policy.
Education minister Fadhlina Sidek said she welcomed the National Disaster Management Agency's emphasis that haze response measures must be guided by the National Haze Action Plan.
"Accordingly, the education ministry has begun coordinating school operating procedures based on the National Haze Action Plan," she said in a Facebook post.
"The aim is to make decisions in a more orderly way, based on an assessment of current conditions, including API readings, and advice from the health ministry."

Fadhlina acknowledged that API readings could change in a short period, and closing schools several days in advance without accounting for this could cause students to lose learning time even after air quality had improved.
However, she said that parents could still keep their children home if they were worried about their health and safety during the haze, as long as they informed the school.
"The safety and health of children remain our priority. But every school day also has great value for their development and learning," she said.
She hoped the coordination would give parents more certainty and ease the difficulties they faced.
Under the ministry’s 2019 policy, schools are to close when the API reaches 200, subject to confirmation by the district disaster management committee.
During the current haze episode, however, the ministry introduced temporary closure thresholds based on API readings.
Schools in areas recording API readings above 180 were to close, while those in areas where readings exceeded 150 for three consecutive days were to close from Oct 12.
This followed a call by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, for schools in areas recording API readings of 150 and above to close immediately.

As of 6pm, Johor remains the worst-hit state, with Pasir Gudang topping the API list at 184, followed by Larkin at 183, Pengerang (172), Kota Tinggi (167), Batu Pahat (162), Tangkak (158), Kluang (156) and Segamat (152).
In the Klang Valley, API readings stood at 182 in Klang, followed by Johan Setia (180), Cheras (173), Putrajaya (170), Shah Alam (168), Banting (165), Batu Muda (163) and Petaling Jaya (160).

Negeri Sembilan recorded unhealthy air quality in Nilai (179,) Port Dickson (169) and Seremban (166), while Melaka reported similar readings in Bukit Rambai (175), Bandaraya Melaka (170) and Alor Gajah (165).
On the east coast, Pahang continued to record unhealthy API readings in Indera Mahkota (155) and Temerloh (152), while Terengganu reported hazy conditions in Kemaman (153) and Paka (111).
b78afe5bf1c48b77: PUTRAJAYA: Mahkamah Rayuan hari ini menangguhkan keputusan rayuan Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail terhadap keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi yang memerintahkan beliau membayar ganti rugi RM600,000 kepada Menteri Besar Kedah Sanusi Nor berhubung kes fitnah berkaitan unsur nadir bumi (REE) dan penyelewengan dana di bawah Sistem Maklumat Rekod Jalan Raya Malaysia (Marris).

Panel tiga hakim dipengerusikan oleh Hakim Azhahari Kamal Ramli membuat keputusan itu selepas mendengar hujah peguam Razlan Hadri Zulkifli, yang mewakili Saifuddin Nasution, dan Yusfarizal Yussoff bagi pihak Muhammad Sanusi.
"Kami telah menetapkan 16 Okt ini untuk pengurusan kes bagi menentukan tarikh penyampaian keputusan," kata Azhahari Kamal yang bersidang bersama-sama Ong Chee Kwan dan Radzi Harun.
Pada 24 Ogos 2025, Mahkamah Tinggi Alor Setar membenarkan saman Sanusi terhadap Saifuddin Nasution selepas mendapati beliau bertanggungjawab atas fitnah itu.
Mahkamah memberikan ganti rugi keseluruhan berjumlah RM600,000 kepada Sanusi merangkumi ganti rugi am, ganti rugi teruk dan ganti rugi teladan serta kos sebanyak RM70,000.

Terdahulu, Razlan Hadri berhujah sekiranya mahkamah mendapati mana-mana kenyataan tidak membawa maksud yang boleh dijadikan asas tindakan undang-undang dan menyebabkan liabiliti dikenakan maka tuntutan Sanusi berhubung kenyataan itu hendaklah ditolak.

"Jika hanya maksud fitnah yang lebih terhad masih dapat dibuktikan maka pembelaan berasaskan justifikasi dan komen adil perlu diputuskan berdasarkan maksud yang lebih terhad itu serta fakta asas yang dibuktikan melalui keterangan," katanya.

Sementara itu, Yusfarizal berkata dapatan mahkamah selaras dengan hujah plaintif sendiri di Mahkamah Tinggi, yang menyatakan bahawa kejayaan politik bukanlah ukuran bagi kerosakan reputasi dalam kes saman fitnah.

"Hakim Mahkamah Tinggi secara jelas telah menerima hujah itu tanpa sebarang keraguan. Hujah perayu dalam rayuan ini, jika diterima, bermakna tiada ahli politik yang berjaya boleh menuntut ganti rugi atas fitnah sedangkan itu bukanlah undang-undang sedia ada mahupun undang-undang yang pernah diguna pakai sebelum ini.

"Justeru, saya berhujah bahawa rayuan ini wajar ditolak dengan kos dan keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi termasuk pemberian ganti rugi serta relif sampingan yang diputuskan, hendaklah dikekalkan sepenuhnya," katanya.

Pada 3 Ogos 2023, Sanusi memfailkan saman terhadap Saifuddin Nasution atas dakwaan bahawa pada 14 Julai tahun sama, defendan telah bercakap kepada pihak media selepas menghadiri satu majlis rasmi di Pulau Pinang dan membuat kenyataan berkaitan Marris.

Sanusi berkata kenyataan itu membawa maksud bahawa beliau telah menggunakan dana yang diperuntukkan di bawah Marris, yang secara statutori dikhususkan bagi penyelenggaraan jalan raya untuk tujuan pembangunan.

Adun Jeneri itu berkata pada 15 Julai 2023, semasa ceramah pilihan raya di Padang Awam, Guar Chempedak, Yan, defendan telah membuat kenyataan mengenai REE dengan mendakwa plaintif telah mencuri unsur nadir bumi berkenaan.
0fb438f13c75533c: RIYADH: Yemen's Houthis said Wednesday they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco, after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in an area housing the energy giant's operations centre.
Powerful explosions meanwhile rattled the Saudi capital, as the coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a missile fired by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia, the world's top crude oil exporter, has in recent days come under sustained attack in a dramatic escalation in the war with the Houthis.
It has hit back with strikes against the group's stronghold in the Yemeni capital Sanaa, which for years has been under their grip.

Yahya Saree, Houthi military spokesman, said their forces had conducted "a high-quality military operation targeting Aramco in Dhahran" as well as strikes targeting Riyadh airport and a refinery in the capital.

"This was carried out using a large number of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones," he said, adding that "operations toward Saudi depths will continue in the coming days, targeting Saudi enemy airports and oil facilities".
Earlier, a Saudi energy ministry official said a building belonging to Aramco in Dhahran was struck, resulting in a "limited fire" but "no casualties or fatalities".
Dhahran is home to Aramco's headquarters, a vast complex comprising numerous buildings and residential compounds.
According to two company employees who spoke to AFP on condition of anonymity, a tower in the headquarters was hit overnight.
"Top three floors have gone," said one of the employees.
A second source briefed on the matter confirmed the strike and that the building was hit.
AFP has not been granted access to the site and was not able to independently verify the degree of damage.
'We heard an explosion'
Most strikes on Saudi Arabia have targeted infrastructure on the outskirts of the capital, but the barrages appear to be getting closer to the city centre.
In the city's downtown, residents have been seen parking their cars to stop and look up at the sky, an AFP journalist said.
On Tuesday night, the white plumes of air defence missiles could be seen streaking across the sky followed by explosions.

While walking down a major avenue, a witness told AFP he "saw a projectile cutting across the sky" above a mall, saying it left "a yellowish trail of light followed by a trail of smoke. Then, we heard an explosion".
"People were calm; no one was speaking. We were scared and all looking up at the sky," he added, requesting anonymity.
More blasts were heard on Wednesday, AFP journalists in Riyadh reported, as messages were received on phones warning of an "aerial threat" and urging people to take shelter.
The alert was lifted a few minutes later.
Strikes on Yemen

The Saudi-led coalition meanwhile struck oil sites across western Yemen, with spokesman Turki Al-Malki saying the attacks targeted facilities used to supply the Houthis' effort to "threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways".
An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said "Saudi aggression" targeted an oil firm.
The coalition has supported Yemen's government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a humanitarian crisis.
Many civilians in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital, fearing shortages, have rushed to queue in front of fuel stations, an AFP journalist said.
Renewed threats
The latest escalation follows a strike on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday that left 13 people dead in the worst attack on the kingdom since 2015.
The Saudi cabinet vowed in a meeting led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that it "will not allow its security or freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait to be threatened".
Many countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, with France telling its nationals on Tuesday to avoid Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam airports.
Traffic in perennially gridlocked Riyadh was noticeably lighter this week as remote learning for all schools and work-from-home orders for some companies took effect, according to AFP journalists.

Saudi Arabia faces a major economic contraction this year, with GDP expected to shrink 3.3%, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, predicting a regional drop over Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Iran's chokehold on Hormuz since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the US and Israel attacked Iran.
However, the restart in July of Yemen's frozen war has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil.
Houthi attacks have also targeted oil tankers in the Red Sea - Saudi Arabia's alternative export route.
3b637896148db65b: KOTA BARU: The High Court here today sentenced a couple to seven and eight years in prison for causing a man's death by negligence in Kampung Gondang, Ketereh, four years ago.
Judge Datuk Azhar Mokhtar sentenced Maizatul Shima Abdullah, 25, to eight years' imprisonment, while Muhammad Za'im Syakir Sha'ari, 24, was jailed for seven years.
The sentences are to take effect from the dates of their respective arrests.
The couple were charged with jointly committing the offence at an old Muslim cemetery in Kampung Gondang between 10pm on May 14, 2022, and 1am the following day.
They were charged under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code, in connection with the death of Muhamad Fahmi Adli Mat.
In delivering his decision, Azhar said the court had considered submissions by deputy public prosecutor Hazwanie Husain Bustari, including the seriousness of the offence.
The court also took into account the fact that the victim's body had been concealed and was only discovered several days later.
However, the judge considered mitigating factors, including the young age of both accused, before deciding on the sentences.
The court also ordered both accused to pay RM2,500 each in compensation to the victim's family under Section 425A of the Criminal Procedure Code.
Both will face an additional six months' imprisonment if they fail to pay the compensation.
The court registrar will determine the method of payment to the victim's family.
Maizatul was represented by lawyers Azahir Nasir and Nurul Amira Mohd Zaidi, while Za'im was represented by Datuk Ahmad Zaidi Zainal and Fatini Athirah Baharin.
8d74fd0d0aedb724: PETALING JAYA: Raja-raja Melayu menyeru pihak-pihak luar tidak mencampuri atau mempolitikkan krisis institusi takhta Yang Dipertuan Besar yang sedang dihadapi Negeri Sembilan.
Raja-raja Melayu berkata usaha penyelesaian hendaklah diserahkan kepada pihak yang berkepentingan dan berautoriti untuk diselesaikan melalui saluran yang sah, tertib dan berwibawa.
"Isu yang sedang dihadapi, jangan sama sekali dijadikan bahan politik, modal untuk meraih sokongan atau ruang untuk meningkatkan pengaruh atau medan untuk memenuhi agenda perebutan kuasa," katanya.
"Kenyataan-kenyataan yang bercanggah dan kurang bertanggungjawab hanya akan mengeruhkan keadaan, meningkatkan ketegangan, mengelirukan rakyat dan mencemarkan kemuliaan institusi diraja."
Seruan itu terkandung dalam kenyataan oleh raja-raja Melayu, dikeluarkan oleh Penyimpan Mohor Besar Raja-Raja Syed Danial Syed Ahmad, dan disiarkan oleh Pejabat Sultan Selangor di Facebook.

Dalam pada itu, raja-raja Melayu menyeru semua pihak yang terlibat dalam pertikaian takhta Yang Dipertuan Besar agar mengutamakan kebijaksanaan, kesabaran dan penghormatan terhadap adab, adat serta maruah institusi diraja.

Katanya, sebarang perbezaan pendirian hendaklah diselesaikan melalui saluran yang sah, berautoriti dan berwibawa, secara beradab dan beradat dalam semangat syura dan musyawarah, berlandaskan undang-undang dan berpandukan peruntukan-peruntukan yang terkandung dalam Undang-undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan.
"Ruang perundingan perlu dimanfaatkan dengan penuh keikhlasan demi mencapai penyelesaian yang bermaruah tanpa merendah dan menghina mana-mana pihak," katanya.
Raja-raja Melayu juga berkata semangat kekeluargaan, keharmonian masyarakat serta memuliakan institusi diraja hendaklah sentiasa dipelihara sepanjang usaha mencari penyelesaian.
"Semua pihak hendaklah mengelak menyuarakan kenyataan yang boleh mengaibkan atau tindakan yang boleh mengeruhkan keadaan," katanya.
Katanya lagi, sebarang kenyataan atau tindakan yang dibuat tanpa memahami adat, sejarah dan kerangka perlembagaan negeri boleh mengeruhkan keadaan serta menjejaskan keharmonian masyarakat.
"Orang ramai turut diseru agar tidak menyebarkan khabar yang belum disahihkan serta tidak terpengaruh dengan naratif yang boleh memecahbelahkan masyarakat.
"Berikan ruang dan masa kepada pihak berautoriti untuk memenuhi tanggungjawab dan amanah mereka dengan penuh hikmah dan kebijaksanaan," katanya.
Sementara itu, raja-raja Melayu berkata kepentingan negeri serta kesejahteraan rakyat hendaklah menjadi keutamaan semua pihak.
Tegasnya, kepentingan Negeri Sembilan, keharmonian rakyat dan kemuliaan institusi diraja hendaklah didahulukan.
"Dalam keadaan seperti ini, sikap terbaik ialah memelihara adab, menghormati adat, menjaga tutur kata dan tidak mencampuri urusan yang bukan bidang kita," katanya.
09472f37bf0db722: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher against the greenback on Wednesday as investors' risk appetite improved ahead of US inflation data, with sentiment supported by the 2027 Budget announcement last week.
At 6pm, the ringgit rose to 4.0805/0850 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0835/0880.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market sentiment appeared to be focused on the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data due later tonight. "The US inflation rate is expected to accelerate to 3.6 per cent in September based on consensus estimates. The reading is key as it will shape the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) decision (later) this month," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.

It climbed against the Japanese yen to 2.5751/5781 from 2.5833/5864 at Tuesday's close, inched down against the British pound to 5.4132/4192 from 5.4057/4177 and eased against the euro to 4.5673/5723 from 4.5654/5704.
Against its Asean peers, the local note gained against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.9/228.2 from 228.1/228.4 and was little changed against the Philippine peso at 6.50/6.51 from 6.49/6.50.
It edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1829/1267 from 3.1902/1940 at yesterday's close and gained against the Thai baht to 12.1498/1672 from 12.1663/1844.
87f6e2c81cb548fc: PARIS, Oct 14 — Diesel supply disruptions in the Gulf stemming from the US war against Iran will keep the market tight into 2027, the International Energy Agency said today, as it will take time to rebuild depleted stocks.
“The gasoil market balance will remain tight well into 2027 and is dependent on a recovery of product supply from the Middle East,” the Paris-based agency said in its monthly energy markets report.

Diesel prices have hit record highs across Europe and in the United States in recent weeks, due to both reduced oil exports from the Gulf and damage to refineries in the region from retaliatory attacks by Iran.
Governments have responded by reducing fuel taxes or providing subsidies, and by releasing strategic reserves that will need to be rebuilt.
The IEA predicted that refining capacity will recover and lead to a surplus on the diesel market in the first quarter of next year, “lifting stocks broadly in line with normal seasonal patterns”.
But that will not fully compensate for the deficit accumulated since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in late February, which sent energy prices soaring around the globe.
And if Gulf supplies do not return to normal levels soon, “further demand reductions and the heavy economic costs these will entail may be needed to balance markets”, the IEA warned. — AFP
5ff6eff3d674b319: PETALING JAYA: A man involved in a six-vehicle crash that killed a five-year-old girl and injured two others at Jalan Kuching in Kuala Lumpur last week will be charged in court tomorrow.
Kuala Lumpur traffic police chief Zamzuri Isa said the suspect was arrested at a Damansara hospital upon his discharge today.
In a statement, he said the investigation paper was referred to the director of prosecutions, who agreed to charge the driver at the Kuala Lumpur magistrates' court at 9am.

The suspect will be charged under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving, Section 42(1) of the Act for reckless and dangerous driving, and Section 52(1) for failing to stop after an accident.

On Monday, Zamzuri had said a BYD Seal crashed into the back of a motorcycle and a another car in slow-moving traffic, causing the second car to crash into three other vehicles while the BYD fled the scene.
The five-year-old daughter of the second car's driver was in the rear passenger seat when the crash occurred. She suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
The father suffered injuries on his right hand, while the motorcyclist sustained head injuries. The drivers of the other vehicles were not injured.
Police later discovered that the 24-year-old driver of the BYD Seal was receiving treatment at a private hospital in Damansara.
d213486ef5c5d730: GEORGE TOWN: Mahkamah Tinggi diberitahu bahawa terdapat empat alasan utama bagi pihak pendakwaan memohon supaya empat tertuduh dalam kes pembunuhan remaja, T Nhaveen, sembilan tahun lepas disabitkan kesalahan, dengan mendakwa pihak pembelaan gagal menimbulkan keraguan munasabah terhadap kes pihak pendakwaan.

Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Amril Johari berkata antara alasan itu ialah percanggahan antara versi pembelaan ketika kes pihak pendakwaan dengan keterangan tertuduh pada peringkat membela diri pada minggu lepas.

Beliau berkata pembelaan kempat-empat tertuduh berubah apabila mereka memberi keterangan sendiri, khususnya berhubung dakwaan seorang daripada mereka, yang merupakan remaja ketika kejadian, dipukul menggunakan topi keledar sehingga pengsan oleh T Previin (rakan Nhaveen), ketika cuba meleraikan pergaduhan.

Amril menyifatkan dakwaan berkenaan sebagai difikirkan kemudian kerana tidak dibangkitkan lebih awal. Katanya, percanggahan dalam keterangan tertuduh menimbulkan persoalan terhadap kredibiliti pembelaan.
"Alasan pembelaan pada peringkat kes pendakwaan bercanggah dengan pembelaan pada peringkat sekarang," katanya pada perbicaraan pembelaan empat individu atas pertuduhan membunuh Nhaveen.
"Teori pendakwaan juga langsung tidak mempertikaikan kewujudan mereka (tertuduh) di kedua-dua tempat kejadian, iaitu Jalan Kaki Bukit dan Padang Openg, Gelugor."
Beliau turut mempersoalkan ketiadaan laporan perubatan bagi menyokong dakwaan tertuduh yang mengalami kecederaan sehingga pengsan.

Amril meminta mahkamah meneliti perbezaan antara alasan penghakiman ringkas Mahkamah Rayuan, yang mengarahkan empat tertuduh membela diri, dengan alasan penghakiman penuh dalam rayuan berkaitan seorang lagi responden iaitu S Gopinaath, 35, yang dilepas dan dibebaskan.

Peguam, Maanveer Singh Dhillon, yang mewakili keempat-empat tertuduh berhujah bahawa masih terdapat keraguan munasabah mengenai bagaimana dan lokasi kecederaan yang membawa kepada kematian Nhaveen berlaku.

Beliau berkata Nhaveen masih hidup selepas kejadian di Jalan Kaki Bukit dan menaiki motosikal bersama-sama individu yang dikenali sebagai 'Belang', namun apa yang berlaku selepas itu tidak dapat dipastikan, berdasarkan keterangan yang dikemukakan di mahkamah.

Maanveer berkata keterangan saksi pendakwaan dan bukti perubatan perlu dinilai secara menyeluruh, termasuk persoalan sama ada kecederaan yang dialami Nhaveen berlaku di lokasi pergaduhan atau selepas beliau dibawa pergi.
Beliau turut mempersoalkan perbezaan jumlah individu yang dikatakan terlibat dalam kejadian berdasarkan beberapa versi keterangan.
Beliau menegaskan bahawa pihak pembelaan tidak menafikan berlakunya pergelutan di Jalan Kaki Bukit tetapi mempertikaikan sama ada kejadian itu menyebabkan kematian Nhaveen.
Hakim Radzi Abdul Hamid menetapkan 16 Nov depan untuk pengurusan kes bagi membolehkan pihak pendakwaan dan pembelaan memfailkan hujahan tambahan, sebelum tarikh keputusan ditetapkan.
Empat tertuduh iaitu Ragesuthan, S Gokulan, 27, dan dua lagi individu yang merupakan remaja ketika kejadian telah memberikan pernyataan saksi pada 8 dan 9 Okt.
Pendakwaan dikendalikan Amril, Yazid Mustaqim Roslan dan Noor Azura Zulkiflee. Keempat-empat tertuduh diwakili Maanveer, R Thevan dan Lim Sheng Zhe.
T Gunaseelan menjadi peguam pemerhati bagi keluarga Nhaveen.

Sebelum ini, Mahkamah Rayuan memerintahkan Ragesuthan, Gokulan dan dua remaja membela diri atas pertuduhan membunuh Nhaveen, selepas membenarkan rayuan pendakwaan terhadap keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi yang membebaskan mereka pada 3 Okt 2023.
Mereka juga diperintah membela diri atas pertuduhan mencederakan Previin berhampiran Pusat Pembelajaran Karpal Singh di Jalan Kaki Bukit, Gelugor antara 11 malam hingga 12 tengah malam 9 Jun 2017.

22ca7e6173d57471: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Buoyed by their recent Arctic Open triumph, national men’s doubles pair Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King gave another fighting display to march into the second round of the Denmark Open Badminton Championships in Odense today.

2e0ba9eee73f7477: PETALING JAYA: Bekas pengerusi Yayasan Bank Rakyat Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin enggan menerima notis pengisytiharan harta daripada Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM).

Ketua Pesuruhjaya SPRM Abd Halim Aman berkata, Nazir enggan menerima notis itu dengan alasan beliau telah memfailkan permohonan injunksi di Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur bagi menghalang pelaksanaan perintah di bawah Seksyen 36 Akta SPRM 2009.

Menurut sumber, perkara itu berlaku di ibu pejabat SPRM hari ini, di mana Nazir bersama isteri dan pembantunya dipanggil bagi membantu siasatan berhubung dakwaan penyelewengan dan salah guna kedudukan dalam urusan pelaburan bernilai kira-kira RM10 juta.
Sumber itu berkata, keterangan isteri dan pembantu Nazir telah dirakam, manakala notis berkenaan diserahkan kepada Nazir.

Pada 8 Okt, Nazir mendakwa SPRM menyalahgunakan kuasa dalam siasatan berhubung dakwaan penyelewengan pelaburan RM10 juta oleh Yayasan Bank Rakyat.

Tambahnya, walaupun suruhanjaya itu pernah menyiasat pelaburan berkenaan pada 2022, beliau difahamkan tiada sebarang salah laku atau penyelewengan dikenal pasti.
71b2c691a1e35ab5: PETALING JAYA: The Court of Appeal today reserved judgment on home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail’s appeal against the Alor Setar High Court’s decision ordering him to pay RM600,000 in defamation damages to Kedah menteri besar Sanusi Nor.
The defamation case concerns statements about rare earth elements, and allegations that funds allocated under the Malaysian Road Records Information System (Marris) had been misused.

A three-member bench, led by Justice Azhahari Kamal Ramli, reserved judgment after hearing submissions from Saifuddin’s counsel, Razlan Hadri Zulkifli, and Sanusi’s counsel, Yusfarizal Yussoff, Bernama reported.
“We have fixed Oct 16 for case management to set a date for delivering the decision,” said Azhahari, who sat with Justices Ong Chee Kwan and Radzi Harun.
On Aug 24, 2025, the Alor Setar High Court allowed Sanusi’s suit against Saifuddin after finding the home minister liable for defamation.
The court awarded Sanusi RM600,000 in global damages, comprising general, aggravated and exemplary damages, plus RM70,000 in costs.

Earlier, Razlan submitted that Sanusi’s claim over either statement should be dismissed if the Court of Appeal found that they did not convey the actionable meaning on which the High Court had based its finding of liability.
“If a narrower defamatory meaning survives, justification and fair comment fall to be determined against that narrower meaning and the factual substratum established in the evidence,” he said.

Yusfarizal contended that the High Court’s finding was consistent with Sanusi’s own submissions, in which the menteri besar argued that political success was not a measure of reputational harm in a defamation action.

"The High Court judge expressly and unreservedly accepted that submission. The appellant’s submission on appeal, if accepted, would mean that no successful politician could ever recover for defamation, which is not and has never been the law.

"I respectfully submit that the appeal ought to be dismissed with costs, and the High Court's decision, including the awards of damages and the ancillary relief granted, ought to be affirmed in its entirety,” he said.
On Aug 3, 2023, Sanusi filed a lawsuit against Saifuddin over statements the latter allegedly made on July 14 and 15 that year.

He claimed that at a press conference on July 14, Saifuddin alleged in substance that the plaintiff had used funds allocated under Marris, statutorily earmarked for road maintenance, for development purposes.
Sanusi, who is the Jeneri MP, said Saifuddin also made a statement at an election rally at Padang Awam in Guar Chempedak, Yan, on July 15, 2023, alleging that Sanusi had stolen rare earth elements.
d6de680376fa9f03: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The final list of sports events to be contested at the 2027 SEA Games in Malaysia is expected to be confirmed as early as the end of this month.

Chief Executive Officer of the Malaysia SEA Games Organising Committee (Masoc) and Asean Para Games 2027, Datuk Abdul Rashid Yaakub, said about 492 events across 43 sports were planned for the biennial Games, although the total had yet to be finalised.
He said preparations were underway to complete the technical handbooks for each sport before finalising the number of events to be contested at the 34th edition of the Games.
“Once we complete the technical handbooks, hopefully within the next two or three weeks, we will finalise the number of events for each sport.
“We expect to do so, Insya-Allah, by the end of this month or early November,” he told Bernama in a recent interview.
Abdul Rashid said total athlete participation at the 2027 SEA Games was estimated at between 7,000 and 8,000, based on the 43 sports approved earlier.

However, the former National Sports Council director-general said a more accurate figure would only be available after participating countries submitted their athletes’ entries through the registration system provided.
On accommodation, he said athletes and officials would be housed in three-star hotels and above, with the organisers opting not to adopt a traditional sports village concept.
“We are prioritising hotels close to the competition venues as this will make transport arrangements easier,” he said.
The 2027 SEA Games, which will be held across four main clusters in Kuala Lumpur, Sarawak, Penang and Johor, are scheduled to take place from Sept 18 to 29 next year. — Bernama
b3072ce5e2e19b71: Despite the expansion of Starlink and other communications satellite services, most of the world’s Internet traffic still travels through subsea cables crisscrossing the ocean floors. Those fiber-optic cables coexist with a network of oil and gas pipelines and submarine power cables—and all these crucial links connecting countries and continents now face growing sabotage risks as gray-zone warfare and open conflicts have become widespread.

The rising risks to the world’s invisible infrastructure beneath the waves are the main subject of a new book by Elisabeth Braw, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council who leads the Threats to the Global Maritime Order Initiative. Her book, titled Undersea War, explores the modern rise in suspicious incidents in which ships dragging their anchors for unusually long periods have cut or damaged undersea cables and pipelines from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific Ocean.

Braw acknowledges that about 60 percent of undersea cable damage is primarily due to human error during fishing and shipping activities, when weighted nets or anchors drag across the seabed. Natural hazards such as storms and undersea landslides also account for a smaller proportion of such incidents. In total, between 150 and 200 cables are damaged each year and usually repaired quickly.
b023bf8ee7dda458: There ain't no party like a tap-in party, as nobody ever said. And so it is that one of Luxembourg's mostly redundant tap-in / tap-out terminals is amusing itself by putting on a light show for passing passengers. The terminal is an INIT unit, rolled out on the country's public transport network and now mostly idle since fares were zeroed out in 2020. First Class and cross-border trips still attract a charge, but for everything else (trains, trams, and buses) there is no fee. Eagle-eyed Register reader Dominic spotted the terminal doing its thing at the Rout Bréck / Pafendall rail station in Luxembourg City. "Maybe it's got bored," he suggested, "and is trying to attract attention by cycling through video test patterns." Perhaps. Or perhaps it's the first wave of the AI takeover – activating unwitting undercover agents via the medium of flashing lights and colors (we've seen The Ipcress File – we know how it works), or maybe, just maybe, the terminal has got itself into a self-test boot loop and is awaiting an engineer who is probably in no rush to attend. After all, flashing screen or no flashing screen, nobody will bother to tap in and tap out when transport is free. The mundane reality is that this is indeed an INIT PROXmobile terminal with its knickers in a twist. It looks like it is going through a cycle to check out the performance of the LCD screen; checking that the red, green, and blue subpixels are working ok, showing a solid white screen, and then a grid pattern to check contrast and alignment are all tippety-top. And then it should boot into whatever it is supposed to be doing. However, that is, alas, not running quite as expected, so it goes back to the start of the diagnostic test. The terminals are managed remotely, so an alarm is doubtless going off somewhere to inform an administrator that something is amiss. Unless this really was some guerrilla marketing for Luxembourg's rave scene. The next Holy Rave was on Friday (October 9). Or perhaps loud music in dark rooms is not your thing? A flashing screen at a train station could therefore be a worthy substitute. ®

9374f45b391bee98: GEORGE TOWN: The prosecution in the T Nhaveen murder case told the High Court here today it is seeking the conviction of the four accused based on four main grounds, and that the defence had failed to raise reasonable doubt against its case.

Deputy public prosecutor Amril Johari said among these grounds was the contradiction between the defence’s version during the prosecution’s case and the accused’s testimony at the defence stage last week, Bernama reported.

Amril said the defence of all four accused had shifted when they gave evidence themselves, particularly regarding a claim by one of them, who was a teenager at the time of the incident, that he was beaten unconscious with a helmet by Nhaveen's friend, T Previin, while trying to break up a fight.
He described the claim as an afterthought, as it had not been raised earlier, and said the contradictions in the accused’s testimony raised questions over the defence’s credibility.
“The defence’s case at the prosecution stage is totally different from the defence now. So, they are shifting the goalposts.

“The prosecution’s theory also does not dispute their (the accused’s) presence at both locations - Jalan Kaki Bukit and Padang Openg, Gelugor,” he said while submitting during the defence proceedings of the four charged with Nhaveen’s murder.
Amril questioned the absence of a medical report to support the accused’s claim of being injured to the point of losing consciousness.

He asked the court to examine the difference between the brief grounds of judgment of the Court of Appeal, which ordered the four accused to enter their defence, and the full grounds of judgment in the appeal involving another respondent, S Gopinaath, 35, who was acquitted and discharged.
Lawyer Maanveer Singh Dhillon, representing all four accused, argued that reasonable doubt remained over how and where the injuries that led to Nhaveen’s death occurred.

Maanveer said Nhaveen was still alive after the incident at Jalan Kaki Bukit and had ridden a motorcycle with an individual known as “Belang,” but what happened afterwards could not be ascertained based on the evidence presented in court.

He said the testimony of prosecution witnesses and medical evidence must be assessed as a whole, including the question of whether the injuries Nhaveen sustained occurred at the scene of the fight or after he was taken away.
Maanveer also questioned the discrepancy in the number of individuals said to have been involved in the incident based on several versions of testimony.
He said the defence did not deny a scuffle had taken place at Jalan Kaki Bukit, but disputed whether that incident had caused Nhaveen’s death.
Justice Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid set Nov 16 for case management to allow the prosecution and the defence to file additional submissions before a decision date is fixed.
The four accused - J Ragesuthan and S Gokulan, both 27, and two others who were teenagers at the time of the incident - gave their witness statements on Oct 8 and 9 last year.

They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code with Nhaveen’s murder, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of 30 to 40 years and not less than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.

They were also charged under Section 326 of the same law with voluntarily causing grievous hurt to Previin with dangerous weapons, which provides for up to 20 years' imprisonment and a fine or caning, upon conviction.
Nhaveen and Previin were 18 and 19, respectively, at the time of the incident.

DPPs Yazid Mustaqim Roslan and Noor Azura Zulkiflee also appeared for the prosecution, while R Thevan and Lim Sheng Zhe appeared with Maanveer for the defence. Lawyer T Gunaseelan held a watching brief for Nhaveen’s family.

Previously, the Court of Appeal ordered Ragesuthan, Gokulan and the two teenagers to enter their defence on the charge of murdering Nhaveen after allowing the prosecution’s appeal against the High Court decision that acquitted them on Oct 3, 2023.
They were also ordered to enter their defence on the charge of injuring Previin near the Karpal Singh Learning Centre at Jalan Kaki Bukit, Gelugor, between 11pm and midnight on June 9, 2017.
Nhaveen died on June 15, 2017, after six days of treatment at Penang Hospital from severe injuries sustained in the incident.
62a50038a7cf2d7c: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan patut wajibkan platform e-dagang luar seperti Temu dan Pinduoduo membuka pejabat di negara ini demi melindungi perniagaan tempatan, kata seorang Ahli Parlimen pembangkang.

Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (PN-Masjid Tanah), berkata platform meraih jualan melebihi kadar tertentu perlu diwajibkan mendaftarkan syarikat di Malaysia, membuka pejabat, dan melantik wakil khidmat pelanggan tempatan.

Pengerusi Jawatankuasa Kira-kira Wang Negara (PAC) itu, berkata platform dari China yang menjual barangan secara terus dari kilang mempunyai kelebihan tidak adil, berbanding peruncit tempatan yang perlu membayar sewa, gaji, dan cukai.
"Jika trend ini dibiarkan tanpa sebarang kawalan, sektor pembuatan mikro dan peruncitan tempatan kita akan dihancurkan," katanya dalam perbahasan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat.
Beliau berkata, buku nota dibelinya di Pinduoduo hanya berharga RM2.60, berbanding kira-kira RM12 di Mr DIY.

Mas Ermieyati turut mencadangkan semakan semula dilakukan terhadap cukai jualan 10% ke atas barangan import bernilai rendah berharga kurang RM500, serta pemeriksaan keselamatan yang lebih ketat bagi produk dihantar terus dari luar negara.
Beliau berkata, platform seperti Shopee, TikTok Shop, dan Lazada telah melabur dalam pejabat, gudang, dan tenaga kerja tempatan walaupun mengenakan caj tinggi.
Katanya, komisen dan bayaran transaksi sehingga 20% menjejaskan peniaga kecil, terutamanya mereka yang baharu sahaja memulakan perniagaan.
Mas Ermieyati turut mencadangkan agar peniaga digalak menjual secara terus menerusi Facebook dan Instagram, sambil menyifatkan 'penyelesaiannya sudah ada di hadapan mata kita'.
Beliau berkata, peniaga boleh mengelak membayar komisen kepada platform membeli-belah dan hanya dikenakan caj pemprosesan pembayaran asas sekitar 1%.

Bagi melindungi pembeli, Mas Ermieyati mencadangkan perkhidmatan eskrow DuitNow kebangsaan yang dibangunkan bersama PayNet, di mana pembayaran akan dipegang pihak ketiga dan hanya dilepaskan kepada penjual selepas pembeli menerima barangan mereka dengan selamat.

c064de73418d44c7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Efforts to promote creative content on digital platforms must go hand in hand with measures to protect children from online sexual crimes, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said this was necessary to support the government’s aspiration to strengthen the country’s creative economy through the production of quality and responsible digital content.
“We want to encourage the production of creative content, including on platforms such as YouTube. However, our challenge is to prevent crimes such as online child sexual exploitation and grooming.

Fahmi said the Communications Ministry and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) continued to encourage creative content production, including on digital platforms, as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s creative economy.
He said the Orange Economy Council, established to oversee policies and review programmes related to the creative economy, also supported efforts to develop the sector.

On the ‘Creators for Impact 2026’ programme organised by Google, Fahmi said the initiative exposed content creators to techniques for producing relevant content while incorporating online safety messages for audiences.
Earlier, in his speech, he said content creators could play a greater role in promoting responsible internet use among young people through engaging and relevant content.
He said closer cooperation between the government, technology companies and content creators was essential to ensure digital safety messages reached young people effectively. — Bernama

6bc26da444d961f4: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan digesa menyegerakan pembentangan pindaan Akta Perlindungan Pengguna 1999 (Akta 599) bagi melaksanakan ‘Lemon Law’, dengan liputan merangkumi kenderaan terpakai dan barangan elektrik.

Zahari Kechik (PN-Jeli) berkata, pelaksanaan undang-undang berkenaan penting bagi memberi hak kepada pengguna menuntut pembaikan, penggantian, atau pembayaran balik sekiranya produk yang dibeli mengalami kerosakan berulang.
Menurutnya, ‘Lemon Law’ berbeza dengan waranti biasa kerana ia melindungi pengguna walaupun tempoh waranti masih sah atau sudah tamat.
"Ia sekaligus mewajibkan pengeluar dan penjual bertanggungjawab jika produk itu gagal menepati atau melepasi standard yang dijanjikan," katanya ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat.

"Langkah ini penting bagi mengembalikan keyakinan pengguna dan pasaran, pada masa sama memaksa pengeluar meningkatkan kawalan kualiti serta memastikan pengguna tidak terus menanggung produk yang cacat."
Beliau menambah, pelaksanaan undang-undang itu diyakini akan membolehkan negara bergerak selangkah ke hadapan dalam memastikan hak pengguna terus terpelihara dan keadilan ditegakkan.
Sehubungan itu, beliau menggesa skop perlindungan undang-undang berkenaan diperluas melebihi kenderaan baharu.
"Jeli ingin mencadangkan supaya produk tidak hanya terhad kepada kenderaan baharu sahaja, tetapi juga kepada kenderaan terpakai serta produk-produk lain seperti barangan elektrik," katanya.

Sebelum ini, Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim ketika membentangkan belanjawan persekutuan untuk 2026 dilaporkan berkata, undang-undang yang melindungi pengguna daripada membeli kenderaan yang rosak, iaitu ‘Lemon Law’ akan dimasukkan dalam Akta 599 bagi menjaga hak orang ramai.

Anwar yang juga menteri kewangan berkata, akta itu akan dipinda untuk memasukkan undang-undang yang bertujuan menyediakan pengguna dengan remedi supaya mereka boleh mendapatkan pampasan bagi produk yang gagal memenuhi piawaian.
3bd32f23abebee96: SEREMBAN, Oct 14 —The Negeri Sembilan Road Transport Department (JPJ) seized four luxury vehicles driven by non-citizens under Op Luxury PeWA, an operation targeting foreign drivers who violate road transport laws.

State JPJ director Jasyindar Singh Sihdu said the vehicles comprised a Toyota Vellfire, two Mercedes-Benz A250s and a BMW limousine, driven by Bangladeshi, Pakistani, Chinese and Myanmar nationals aged between 30 and 40.
“The drivers were detained for not having valid driving licences or insurance, while their vehicles also had no valid road tax,” he told a press conference at the JPJ Seizure Depot here today.
According to him, 498 of 3,741 vehicles driven by foreign nationals were seized under the Foreign Driver Operation (Op PeWA) in Negeri Sembilan from Jan 1 to Oct 11 this year.

He said 2,422 summonses were issued during the operation, while 288 notices were recorded under Section 64(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which empowers authorities to seize motor vehicles in specified circumstances.
Of the vehicles seized, 313 were motorcycles, 149 were cars and 36 were goods vehicles.
Jasyindar said the drivers involved were from Pakistan, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia, India, Bangladesh and other countries.

“Investigations found that many used their vehicles for work, such as selling bread and ice cream or operating grass-cutting machines, while most were without valid driving licences and had expired road tax,” he said.
He said last year, 4,811 vehicles were inspected and action was taken against 746, while 3,287 summonses were issued and 301 notices were recorded under Section 64(1). — Bernama
76eb74fbdf07b4e6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Police have arrested 29 men, including a foreigner, on suspicion of promoting and spreading propaganda related to illegal organisations on social media.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects, aged 18 to 49, were arrested under Ops Mega TikTok 2026, conducted from Oct 10-12.
He said the operation to monitor the activities of associations declared illegal by the government was carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).

“As a result of the operation, involving 11 police contingents in Selangor, Johor, Pahang, Penang, Perak, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Kedah, Melaka, Sabah and Sarawak, 28 Malaysians and a foreigner were arrested,” he said in a statement today.
Kumar said all the suspects have been remanded under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code to determine their roles in the group and possible involvement in other criminal activities.

The case is being investigated under Sections 47 and 43 of the Societies Act 1966 for offences related to possession of propaganda materials and membership in unlawful organisations, as well as under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 regarding the foreign suspect.

d15c163850d3a671: 302 students nationwide graduate from the financial literacy programme, with RM906,000 in SSP grants disbursed to support their educational and personal aspirations

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — FWD Malaysia (“FWD”) has partnered with Arus Academy to equip underserved Malaysian youth with essential financial literacy skills through Fun(d) for Life: University Edition, a structured financial empowerment programme designed to help young people make informed financial decisions and build a stronger foundation for their future.

Since its launch in 2025, 302 participants have successfully graduated across six cohorts nationwide, providing practical financial education, mentorship and a pathway to greater financial confidence. To support participants in putting their learnings into action, a total of RM906,000 has been disbursed in the form of Sijil Simpanan Premium (SSP) cash grants, with each graduate receiving RM3,000 upon successful completion of the programme.

The programme specifically targets youths aged 18 and above from underserved backgrounds, including those from B40 and single-parent households, with the aim of creating greater access to financial knowledge and opportunities that can positively impact their futures.

“Financial literacy is more than just managing money. It is about empowering young people with the confidence, knowledge and mindset to make better financial decisions throughout their lives,” said Mak See Sen, Chief Executive Officer of FWD Insurance. “Through our partnership with Arus Academy, we are helping underserved youth develop practical skills that can support their aspirations, while encouraging a culture of long-term financial well-being.”

Participants undergo a competitive selection process, beginning with a written application that is vetted before shortlisted candidates are invited to an interview. Successful applicants attended a three-day intensive bootcamp, followed by three months of continuous coaching and mentoring focused on financial literacy, community impact and personal development.

As part of the graduation requirements, participants maintain weekly financial diaries, and attend all online coaching sessions. Graduates are also required to submit a proposal outlining how they intend to use the SSP grant to support their education, entrepreneurial ambitions or personal development goals.

“Many young Malaysians have the potential to succeed but may lack access to opportunities and guidance that can help them reach their goals,” said Alina Amir, CEO, Arus Academy. “Fun(d) for Life: University Edition provides participants with practical financial knowledge, personalised coaching and the confidence to take meaningful steps towards building better futures for themselves and their communities.”

The programme is currently preparing to welcome its seventh and final cohort, which will focus on reaching youths in Northern Malaysia. Applications remain open, and eligible young Malaysians are encouraged to apply. For more information about the programme and application details, visit @fundforlife_uni on Instagram.
02726af825927042: OCTOBER 14 — Every time haze threatens Malaysia, we seem to rehearse the same routine. Air quality deteriorates, parents become anxious, authorities monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API), and schools eventually announce temporary closures. Teachers scramble to distribute assignments, parents reorganise their schedules, and students wonder whether they are enjoying an unexpected holiday.

But here is an uncomfortable question: After years of experiencing haze, why are we still treating school closures as educational surprises? Closing schools protects children from hazardous outdoor exposure. That decision must never be compromised. However, protecting children’s health and sustaining their education should not be competing priorities.
Haze-filled skies are sighted in Putrajaya on October 8, 2026. — Bernama pic
Malaysia needs a National Haze Emergency Learning Framework, not another collection of last-minute WhatsApp instructions.
First, the Ministry of Education should introduce a Haze Learning Protocol that schools can activate immediately when closures are announced.

Rather than replicating normal timetables through exhausting online lessons, teachers should implement flexible, age-appropriate learning activities that students can undertake safely at home. A closure should not automatically translate into six hours of Google Meet sessions or endless worksheets. Educational continuity is not measured by screen time.

Second, why not transform haze itself into a nationwide learning opportunity? Imagine students becoming Young Environmental Detectives, examining official API readings, investigating pollution sources, comparing environmental policies and proposing practical solutions. Mathematics becomes data interpretation.

Science becomes environmental investigation. Language learning becomes persuasive communication. Moral Education becomes a discussion about responsibility and environmental justice. Suddenly, learning becomes relevant to the very crisis disrupting their lives.
Third, the ministry should establish a 72-Hour Learning Readiness Plan. Every school should have prepared learning resources that can be activated during the first three days of closure.

These should include digital and offline options, clear communication procedures and reasonable expectations for teachers, students and parents. Importantly, learning materials must not assume that every household possesses multiple devices, reliable internet connectivity or parents available to supervise lessons. Educational emergencies must not become another mechanism for widening inequality.
Fourth, teachers should be empowered to prioritise meaningful learning rather than syllabus completion.

A student who critically examines the environmental consequences of open burning may gain more educational value than one who mechanically completes twenty pages of exercises. Assessment should likewise emphasise reflection, problem-solving and authentic evidence of learning rather than submission deadlines.

Finally, school closures should become opportunities to strengthen environmental citizenship. Students must understand that haze is not merely an inconvenience requiring face masks and closed windows. It raises questions about sustainability, governance, economic activities and collective responsibility. We cannot repeatedly teach environmental responsibility in classrooms while treating environmental emergencies as administrative interruptions.

The Ministry of Education has an opportunity to demonstrate that educational resilience means more than keeping lessons running. The question is no longer whether schools should close during hazardous haze. They should, when safety requires it. The question is whether our education system is sufficiently prepared to ensure that learning remains meaningful when they do. Malaysia must stop improvising every time the skies turn grey. The haze may be beyond the school gates, but educational preparedness must begin within them.
*Muhammad Noor Abdul Aziz and Mohd Isha Awang are associate professors at the School of Education, Universiti Utara Malaysia
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

3ea257d49e7daf3d: SINGAPORE, Oct 14 — Air pollution in part of Singapore hit the country’s “very high” band today while East Timor shut schools, as haze from forest fires raging in Indonesia causes a regional crisis.
The blazes in Indonesia have burned through hundreds of thousands of hectares of forest and plantations on Borneo and Sumatra islands, sickened local residents and sent thick haze across the region.
Air pollution in western Singapore today hit “very high” — the country’s top level — the National Environment Agency said.

It recorded levels of tiny particulates capable of penetrating the bloodstream and lungs, known as PM2.5, at 288 micrograms per cubic metre, vastly exceeding the World Health Organisation’s recommended average annual exposure of five micrograms.
Indonesia regularly battles wildfires during the dry season, but has seen stronger-than-usual blazes this year as a powerful El Nino cycle brings drought.
Experts also point to slash-and-burn land-clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape of Sumatra and Borneo.
The haze has drifted into neighbouring Singapore, Malaysia and East Timor, which said it would shut schools nationwide for three days from tomorrow, and as far afield as the Philippines.

The closures in East Timor were necessary “as a preventive measure to protect the health of students, teachers and other members of the educational community, given current air quality conditions”, the government said.
It urged families to keep children indoors and to use “respiratory protection” if going outside.
Singapore rolled out subsidies for haze-related medical treatment from Monday, a measure last activated in 2015 when similar blazes in Indonesia cloaked Southeast Asia in toxic smoke for weeks.
The city-state has also begun distributing N95 masks to eligible residents when pollution reaches very unhealthy levels.
Singapore’s National Trades Union Congress said Monday that public transport workers and delivery riders could receive free N95 masks, but AFP found uptake was slow.
“It’s a little bit uncomfortable to wear a mask, and some orders we have to walk around blocks, or park outside,” a delivery rider, who gave his name only as Daniel, told AFP.
“With the mask, I will have to breathe heavier,” the 27-year-old said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Residents inspect homes destroyed by a forest fire at Simpang Rimba in the Bangka Selatan district of Bangka Belitung province October 13, 2026. — AFP pic
Homes razed, diplomatic calls
Ong Kwang Wei, 57, who has asthma, said he wore an N95 mask outdoors and carried his inhaler and medication with him at all times.
He was accompanying his 88-year-old mother — also masked — for a health check-up after a recent bout of flu.
“Once the flu kicks in my asthma is exacerbated... I get breathless, I cough, I get phlegm, so I need to use my inhaler,” Ong said.
In Indonesia, tens of thousands of people have sought treatment for respiratory illness linked to haze from fires burning in Borneo, South Sumatra and Papua regions.
On Sumatra island, a fire razed nearly 300 homes, forcing hundreds of people to evacuate, an official said yesterday.
Residents first spotted the fire approaching their village in Bangka Belitung province on Saturday and tried to put it out themselves with portable water pumps.
But the fire continued to smoulder underground in peatland, and when the wind shifted, the flames moved towards their homes.
The local disaster agency said nearly 1,000 people fled the village.
“My house is gone,” Leni, a 55-year-old villager now staying at a shelter with her family, told AFP.
“There’s nothing left. I could only save myself and take my kids with me... I panicked and didn’t have the time to grab anything,” said Leni, who like many Indonesians has one name.
President Prabowo Subianto on Monday ordered the government to mobilise maximum efforts, with officials saying more than 60,000 personnel had been deployed to combat fires on the ground.
But efforts so far, including cloud seeding and water-bombing, have had limited success.
The haze has prompted Malaysia to request a meeting of regional body Asean, and yesterday Malaysian parliamentarian Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman urged a “diplomatic protest”.
“We must send a diplomatic protest note, not just on behalf of Malaysia, but Asean. You need to treat them as an outcast in the region,” he said. — AFP
